If you have the Atmos™ Rewards Ascent Visa Signature® credit card or the Atmos™ Rewards Summit Visa Infinite® credit card, you can earn 3 Atmos Rewards points for every dollar spent on eligible rent when paying through Bilt, on up to $50,000 per calendar year; terms apply. Related: The best credit cards for Alaska Airlines flyers American Airlines is a transfer partner of Citi ThankYou, so you can transfer points to your AAdvantage account if you have one of the following cards: - Citi Strata Elite℠ Card (see rates and fees): Best for Citi Travel users and American Airlines flyers - Citi Strata Premier® Card (see rates and fees): Best for earning full-fledged ThankYou Rewards points with a low annual fee - Citi Prestige® Card: Best for restaurants, airlines and travel agencies The information for the Citi Prestige Card has been collected independently by The Points Guy. The card details on this page have not been reviewed or provided by the card issuer. You also might want to check out one of the following American Airlines cobranded cards to rack up miles quickly with a large welcome offer and keep your account stocked thanks to earning miles on everyday spending: The information for the Citi AAdvantage Platinum Select has been collected independently by The Points Guy. The card details on this page have not been reviewed or provided by the card issuer. Related: The best credit cards for American Airlines flyers Use Virgin Atlantic Flying Club and Flying Blue miles for Delta flights Delta flies to Liberia, Costa Rica from its megahub at Atlanta's Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport (ATL). The airline also recently announced it would be relaunching weekly nonstop service from JFK from Dec. 19, 2026-Apr. 10, 2027. The Delta SkyMiles program prices awards dynamically, so the higher the cost of airfare, the more miles you'll need for tickets. However, the airline is also partners with other carriers including Virgin Atlantic and Air France-KLM, so you can often find lower-priced awards using miles from their loyalty programs instead of SkyMiles. For instance, this flight from Atlanta to Liberia would cost 31,700 SkyMiles plus $25 in taxes and fees in economy. But it would only cost 18,500 Virgin Atlantic miles plus the same taxes and fees. Even better, Air France-KLM Flying Blue would only charge you 16,500 miles, though the taxes and fees are $52. Still, that could be worth it to save nearly half your miles compared to using Delta SkyMiles! Virgin Atlantic Flying Club is a 1:1 transfer partner of: Flying Blue, meanwhile is a 1:1 transfer partner of: Even if you don't regularly fly Virgin or Air France-KLM, or fly Delta for that matter, you have tons of ways to top up your frequent-flyer accounts. Book United flights using Air Canada Aeroplan points United Airlines flies nonstop to Liberia from its major hubs, including: - Chicago O'Hare International Airport (ORD) - Denver International Airport (DEN) - Houston's George Bush Intercontinental Airport (IAH) - Newark Liberty International Airport (EWR) United MileagePlus prices award tickets dynamically based on airfare, too, so the more tickets cost, the more miles you can expect to redeem. That's why it pays to keep Air Canada's Aeroplan program in mind since you can redeem Aeroplan points for United flights. For instance, this flight from Chicago to Liberia requires just 15,000 Aeroplan points. But the same flight would cost 20,000 United MileagePlus miles, unless you have elite status or a cobranded United credit card. That's the lowest price discrepancy I could find — typically, United flights to Costa Rica start closer to 22,500 miles each way. Now, the taxes and fees on United MileagePlus awards are just about $80 round-trip, versus $180 with Aeroplan, but it could be worth spending the extra cash to save miles, as well as the fact that round-trip airfares on this route typically run anywhere from $760-$2,200 over the next several months. Also keep in mind that if you do have elite status or a cobranded United Credit card, that you often have access to award prices that are cheaper than general MileagePlus members. That 20,000-mile award drops down to 18,000 miles, so be sure you're logged into your account to see what pricing is available to you. United is transfer partners with Chase Ultimate Rewards and Bilt, so even if you don't fly the airline regularly or have a United credit card, there are plenty of ways to stock up on miles. Air Canada Aeroplan is a transfer partner of: Whether you want to go with United miles or Aeroplan points, you have plenty of options for stocking up on them. Related: The best United credit cards Stay true (blue) to JetBlue For East Coasters, JetBlue is also a contender since it flies to Costa Rica from its hubs at: - Boston Logan International Airport (BOS) - Fort Lauderdale-Hollywood International Airport (FLL) - New York-JFK Even better, the airline's flights can be downright bargains when redeeming its own JetBlue TrueBlue points. You can find flights from JFK, in particular, for as few as 11,900 TrueBlue points plus $24-$63 each way instead of $195-$229. Like Delta and United, JetBlue prices awards dynamically based on airfares, but you can count on a solid fixed value per point of about 1.4 cents apiece. JetBlue is a transfer partner of the following programs at the following ratios: - American Express Membership Rewards (250:200), - Chase Ultimate Rewards (1:1) - Citi ThankYou Rewards (Varies from 1,000:700 to 1,000:1,000 depending on your card) Related: The best credit card for JetBlue flyers Use Marriott points at these Costa Rica hotels There's no shortage of resorts where you can redeem Marriott Bonvoy points to save on hotel rates. You can stretch your points and your budget even further by redeeming points for all-inclusive hotels. While this is not an exhaustive list, here are three great Marriott-affiliated hotels where your points can come in handy. The Westin Reserva Conchal, an All-Inclusive Golf Resort & Spa is a favorite with families and couples alike since it has an adults-only area and one for guests of all ages as well as dreamy pools and a beach club. Guests can also enjoy over a dozen bars and restaurants serving everything from tapas and pizza to Asian fusion and seafood. Rates at the Westin Reserva Conchal start at $512 or 88,000 Marriott Bonvoy points per night. For something a little sultrier, you can opt for the nearby W Costa Rica-Reserva Conchal, which has just 132 rooms and 18 suites, for a more intimate, design-forward feel. While away an afternoon in one of the poolside cabanas or relaxing at the Away Spa and then celebrate with a predinner cocktail at the seaglass-inspired Living Room and dinner at the lively Zona Azul Beach Club. Rates at the W Costa Rica start at $350 or 59,000 Marriott Bonvoy points per night. Marriott's latest Costa Rica resort will open later this fall. The JW Marriott Costa Elena Resort & Spa is a sophisticated new all-inclusive making its debut along the Guanacaste coast with 415 rooms and suites and a 44,000-square-foot pool among its hallmarks. Guests will also find 11 bars and restaurants and a huge spa. Rates at the JW Marriott Costa Elena start at $580 or 112,000 Marriott Bonvoy points per night. Related: The best Marriott credit cards Use Hilton points at these Costa Rica hotels Hilton points turn out to be versatile whether you want to stay near the beach or up in the mountains. One of the most exciting recent additions to Costa Rica's hotel scene in recent memory is the Waldorf Astoria Costa Rica Punta Cacique, perched above beautiful Culebra Bay, about a 45-minute drive from Liberia's international airport. The resort comprises 148 guest rooms and 40 suites spanning 20 room types, so there are choices for every configuration. The hotel also offers several distinct restaurants, including Tico Tica for seafood and pasta, La Finca for upscale Costa Rican cuisine and, of course, an outpost of Waldorf's signature Peacock Alley for coffee, tea and cocktails. The Waldorf Astoria Spa is another selling point in its favor. Rates at the Waldorf Astoria Costa Rica start at $622 or 120,000 Hilton Honors points per night. Looking for something a little more niche? Remember that you can also redeem Hilton Honors points at many boutique lodges thanks to the program's partnership with Small Luxury Hotels, including the captivating Rio Perdido, which has just 38 stilted bungalows constructed of timber and volcanic stone and surrounded by lush jungle on a 1,500-acre reserve. Guests can go on wildlife hikes, zipline through the forest and swim in a geothermal river, among other distinctive activities. Rates at Rio Perdido start at $290 or 90,000 Hilton Honors points per night. Related: The best Hilton credit cards Use Hyatt points at these Costa Rica hotels Hyatt beckons with classic beach retreats as well as more unique offerings thanks to its acquisition of Mr & Mrs Smith. One of TPG staffers' all-time favorite Hyatt redemptions is the beautiful Andaz Costa Rica Resort at Peninsula Papagayo, located in a lush private development along Culebra Bay, just 45 minutes from Liberia. The hotel sprawls along a ridgeline overlooking the inlet and features a swanky cocktail bar, high-end restaurants, a peaceful little spa and plenty of pools, not to mention a private beach club to which guests can catch a free shuttle boat. Rates at the Andaz Papagayo start at $512 or 35,000 World of Hyatt points per night. Prefer an all-inclusive where you don't have to watch your dining budget? Consider the adults-only Secrets Papagayo Costa Rica, which has a more casual, but still intimate feel with just 202 rooms and suites, not to mention a beautiful oceanfront location. The hotel has a whopping 12 bars and restaurants, including an alfresco deck with a health-focused menu, a pan-Asian eatery and an Italian cucina. Rates at Secrets Papagayo start at $560 or 25,000 Hyatt points per night. Finally, for a nature-filled, off-the-grid experience in the heart of Costa Rica's rainforest, consider a visit to Origins Lodge, which is tucked up in the highlands near the country's northern border with vistas that stretch all the way to Nicaragua, about 90 minutes' drive from Liberia. The hillside bungalows are at one with their surroundings, with plenty of natural light as well as private decks with woodfired jacuzzis. Guests can enjoy gourmet meals of locally-sourced ingredients with daily changing menus in between activities like guided nature hikes to spot sloths and visit thundering waterfalls, horseback rides, whitewater rafting and more. Rates at Origins Lodge start at $885 or 76,750 World of Hyatt points per night. Related: Which credit cards should you use for Hyatt stays? Avoid resort fees when redeeming hotel points in Costa Rica Unfortunately, resort fees are a fact of life and can add hundreds of dollars to your trip cost depending on the hotel and the length of your stay. Sure, $30-$40 extra per day might not break the bank, but some resorts charge much, much more than that. The Waldorf Astoria Punta Cacique, for instance, charges a 12% mandatory daily fee. On rates that tend to hover around $1,250, that's an extra $150 per day! Luckily, Hilton Honors and World of Hyatt waive resort fees on award stays, so you might want to consider those programs first if you're going to redeem points for a hotel on your trip. Related: The 13 best all-inclusive resorts in Costa Rica for beach visits or hiking trips Save on luxury stays with premium card credits There are plenty of very high-end hotels to stay in Costa Rica, and Guanacaste in particular. If you are considering resorts on the costlier side of the budget spectrum, it could be worth taking a look at the cards in your wallet and whether they open up possibilities for booking (and saving) through the issuer's hotel booking portal. For instance, folks with either the American Express Platinum Card® or The Business Platinum Card® from American Express, you can book American Express Fine Hotels + Resorts properties and get up to $300 back in statement credits semiannually for up to a total of $600 per year on prepaid Fine Hotels + Resorts or The Hotel Collection bookings (of two nights or more for the latter) through American Express Travel. Not only that, but by booking through FHR, you also receive benefits like availability-based upgrades, complimentary daily breakfast for two and a $100 credit to use for on-property charges like meals or spa treatments, so you can end up saving even more. That can come in handy at a hotel like Nekajui, a Ritz-Carlton Reserve, where room rates are already high and redeeming Marriott points can come at exorbitant levels. Similarly, if you have the Chase Sapphire Reserve® (see rates and fees) or the Chase Sapphire Reserve for Business℠ (see rates and fees) and book a hotel that is part of The Edit by Chase Travel℠, such as the longstanding favorite Four Seasons Resort Peninsula Papagayo, Costa Rica, you are eligible for two statement credits of up to $250 each (for a total of $500) this calendar year to put toward stays of two nights or more. During your stay, you are also eligible for availability-based upgrades, complimentary daily breakfast and a $100 on-property credit. Related: Our favorite American Express Fine Hotels + Resorts around the world Use points toward activities While we often suggest redeeming points for flights and hotel nights to get the most value, don't forget that you can use certain types of points and miles for activities, in addition to travel. For example, you can redeem your Capital One miles from a card like the Capital One Venture X Rewards Credit Card or the Capital One Venture Rewards Credit Card at a rate of one cent apiece for experiences like a kayak and snorkeling trip around Culebra Bay near Papagayo, or a full-day volcano zipline, horseback ride and whitewater tubing experience in the nearby mountains. If you have a card that earns Chase Ultimate Rewards points, like the Chase Sapphire Reserve or the Chase Sapphire Preferred® Card (see rates and fees), you can also redeem them at one cent apiece for activities like a catamaran sailing and snorkeling tour, or a horseback ride along Conchal Beach. Are these the highest-value redemptions? No. But if they help you create a memorable experience for yourself and your loved ones during your trip — and save you money — then, why not? Rental car documentation in Costa Rica If you want to cover some ground during your time in Costa Rica, you might consider renting a car. Especially because doing so might be cheaper than paying for your hotel's airport shuttle, and once you get to your accommodations, many resorts provide free parking. However, car rentals in Costa Rica work a little differently than in the U.S., and many other countries, for that matter. That's because you must — no getting out of it — purchase third-party liability insurance from the Instituto Nacional de Seguros, which covers damage and injuries to third parties, but does not cover you or your vehicle. It costs around $10-$20 per day. Then, unlike pretty much anywhere else you rent, just using a credit card to pay for your rental that provides primary or secondary insurance is not enough, either. Some agencies will still require you to purchase their own collision damage and liability insurance, so call ahead to see if you need to factor that in. If you do find an agency that will allow you to rely on your own credit card insurance (Alamo and Avis should let you do so), then you will still need to obtain a formal letter from your credit card stating that your rental will be covered by their insurance. A call to your card's customer service phone number should suffice, then they will email you a letter that you can print and take with you. It's a rigmarole, but worth saving hundreds of dollars over the course of even a short rental. Related: Credit card rental car insurance: Best cards and how it works Bottom line Costa Rica is truly one of the world's most versatile destinations, with something for everyone, whether it's a relaxing beach vacation, a laidback surf trip, an adrenaline-inducing adventure in the jungle or a wildlife-filled rainforest experience. There are also plenty of ways your points and miles can help you save on a trip there, so bookmark this page and come back to it for ideas. And, if you have more questions or tips of your own, feel free to share those in the comments! Frequently asked questions Many of Costa Rica’s major resorts are located along the country’s Pacific coast. The area around Guanacaste, which is served by Daniel Oduber Quirós International Airport (LIR), in particular, has plenty of all-inclusive and luxury resorts including the Andaz Peninsula Papagayo Resort, Costa Rica, by Hyatt and the new Waldorf Astoria Costa Rica Punta Cacique. You can also venture up into the national parks of the north and south for a more jungly trip where adventure and wildlife are the main attractions. The best time to visit Costa Rica is from December through April, with the most temperate, sunniest months being January through March. For fewer crowds, consider a visit during the “green season” of May through November, when temperatures can be higher and there is typically a chance of rain. The number of miles you need to fly to Costa Rica depends on which airline you take and which miles you redeem, as well as the time of year since some mileage program require more miles during peak travel times. That said, you can find flights on some airlines, like American, by redeeming as few as 7,500 miles each way. You can find flights to Costa Rica on all the major U.S. airlines including Alaska Airlines, American Airlines, Delta Air Lines, JetBlue, Southwest and United. The cost of a trip to Costa Rica depends on when you visit, how long your trip is and where you want to stay. The country has options for travelers ranging from budget flights and accommodations to luxury resorts and rainforest lodges that can cost well over $1,000 a night. Luckily, many hotels in the country are accessible using credit card rewards and hotel points.

item.title: Bank of America Travel Center guide: How to book travel and redeem rewards
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 5.05
Bank of America Travel Center guide: How to book travel and redeem rewards If you didn't know Bank of America had a travel portal, you're probably not alone. The Bank of America Travel Center doesn't get nearly as much attention as travel portals from issuers like Chase, Capital One and Citi. But there's more to BofA Travel than you might expect, including plenty of ways to book travel and use your rewards. Here's how the portal works and what to know before you book. What is the Bank of America Travel Center? The Bank of America Travel Center — which you'll see referred to as BofA Travel within the booking experience — lets eligible cardholders book flights, hotels, rental cars and activities. Bank of America revamped the Travel Center in July 2026. The new portal, powered by Rocket Travel by Agoda, significantly expanded the selection of hotels, flights, rental cars and activities available to book. The update wasn't just cosmetic. Now, the portal has better search and filtering tools, more detailed hotel information and the ability to mix and match airlines on round-trip bookings. Eligible cardholders can even combine rewards with a credit or debit card payment. Who can access the Bank of America Travel Center? Exactly what you can do in the Travel Center depends on which Bank of America card is in your wallet. Some cardholders can book travel and redeem rewards through the portal, while others can only make paid bookings. How you access the Travel Center varies by card, too. Here's what access currently looks like for eligible personal Bank of America cards: | Card | Booking and payment options | Where to find BofA Travel | |---|---|---| | | Book with rewards and/or card payments | Online Banking or mobile app | | | Book with rewards and/or card payments | Online Banking or mobile app | | | Book with card payments | Online Banking | | | Book with card payments | Erica in the mobile app or Search in Online Banking | | | Book with card payments | Erica in the mobile app or Search in Online Banking | | BankAmericard Rewards® credit card (closed to new applicants) | Book with rewards and/or card payments | Online Banking | The information for the BankAmericard Rewards credit card and Bank of America Premium Rewards Elite credit card has been collected independently by The Points Guy. The card details on this page have not been reviewed or provided by the card issuer. Related: Best Bank of America credit cards of September 2026 How to use the Bank of America Travel Center Once you're in BofA Travel, here's what to expect when making a booking. How to book flights through the Bank of America Travel Center To search for flights, enter your origin, destination, travel dates and number of travelers. BofA Travel supports one-way, round-trip and multicity searches, and you can search by economy, premium economy, business or first class. Once your results load, you can filter your options and compare flights from more than 170 airlines. On round-trip itineraries, your outbound and return flights don't need to be on the same carrier. Each flight includes a tab with baggage information and a link to the airline's baggage policies. Pay close attention to the fare you're selecting, since restrictions and included benefits vary by fare type. There can be some airline-specific quirks, too. When I selected a Frontier Airlines flight, BofA Travel warned me that the flight would be managed directly by Frontier and that I'd need to contact the airline for any changes or assistance after booking. You also can't select your seat before booking, at least for the airlines I tested, which included Frontier, American Airlines, Delta Air Lines and United Airlines. Each time, the booking page told me I'd need to contact the airline for seat selection. Don't forget to add your frequent flyer number during booking, since flights booked through BofA Travel can still earn airline miles and elite-qualifying credits based on the airline's fare rules. Once you've entered your information and reviewed your flight and fare details, select "Continue to payment" to finish booking. How to book hotels through the Bank of America Travel Center To search for a hotel, select "Hotels" and enter your destination, travel dates and number of travelers. Then hit "Search hotels." There are more than half a million properties available worldwide, ranging from traditional hotels to apartments, hostels and other accommodations. So, whether you're looking for a five-star hotel, a budget stay or something with more space, you'll probably find an option that fits. Once your results load, you'll see a surprisingly extensive list of filters. You can narrow properties by neighborhood, star and guest ratings, amenities, bed type, hotel brand and proximity to popular attractions. There are also filters for specific room offers, such as free cancellation or included breakfast. For example, when I searched for a stay in Paris, I could narrow my results to specific neighborhoods like the Champs-Élysées, Montmartre and the area around the Louvre. I could even filter by nearby attractions, such as the Arc de Triomphe or Palais Garnier. Search results show both the cash and points price for eligible cardholders. For example, the Hotel Du Louvre, Part Of Hyatt, was listed for $646 or 61,842 points plus $27. On the final booking page, BofA Travel breaks down the total price, including any taxes and fees or amounts due at the property. You can also review the room details and cancellation policy before continuing to payment. How to book rental cars through the Bank of America Travel Center To search for a rental car, enter your pickup and drop-off locations, dates and times, as well as the driver's age. Once your results load, you can filter by pickup location, rental agency, vehicle type and transmission. Eligible cardholders will see both the cash and points cost in the search results. In the searches I tried, that price stayed the same all the way through checkout. That's a nicer feature than it might sound. I've booked plenty of one-way rental cars where the drop-off fee wasn't shown during booking, or I wasn't even warned there would be one. Seeing that cost upfront makes it much easier to know what you'll actually pay. Before paying for your reservation, you can (and should) review the rental company's policies by opening the "Read agency policies" tab. This includes important information about age and payment requirements, deposits, insurance, additional drivers and other rental-specific rules. Cancellation and payment policies vary by reservation; for example, one rate I checked was nonrefundable, nontransferable and couldn't be changed. How to book activities through the Bank of America Travel Center Activities and experiences are available through the portal, too. Just search by city or attraction to see what's available. From there, you can browse tours, transportation, attractions, experiences, food and travel essentials. You can also filter results by price, star rating, duration and category or sort them by popularity, price or rating. Select an activity to see the available booking options and more detailed information, including departure and return details, what to expect, additional information and the cancellation policy. Pay attention to how each activity is priced. For example, the private Paris airport transfer I looked at was priced for up to two people rather than per person, and the displayed price included all taxes and fees. How to redeem rewards through the Bank of America Travel Center Eligible cardholders can redeem Bank of America rewards toward bookings through BofA Travel. You don't need enough rewards to cover the entire cost, either. You can pay with rewards, combine rewards with a credit or debit card or pay entirely by card. Bank of America says these redemption options vary by card and will expand over time. BofA Rewards points are worth at least 1 cent each when redeemed through BofA Travel. That means 50,000 points would cover at least $500 in flights, hotels, rental cars or activities. However, some cardholders can get even more value from their points. For example, the Premium Rewards Elite carries a hefty $550 annual fee, but if you're a frequent BofA Travel user, you can make up some ground with one particularly valuable perk: a 20% discount when redeeming points for airfare. For example, a $1,000 flight that would normally require 100,000 points costs just 80,000 points — a value of 1.25 cents per point. The discount also applies to the portion of airfare paid with points when you combine points and a card payment. Should you book through the Bank of America Travel Center? There are some good reasons to book through BofA Travel. But the portal won't make sense for every booking — and depending on how you travel, one of the best travel rewards credit cards from another issuer could potentially offer more value. When it makes sense to book through the BofA Travel Center Consider booking through BofA Travel when: - You want to redeem BofA Rewards points for travel. Eligible cardholders can use points toward flights, hotels, rental cars and activities, or combine points with a credit or debit card payment. - You have the Premium Rewards Elite card. Cardholders get a 20% points discount when redeeming rewards for airfare through BofA Travel. - Your card earns bonus rewards through the Travel Center. Some Bank of America cards offer elevated earning rates on eligible Travel Center purchases. - You're booking an independent hotel. You won't be giving up chain-specific hotel points, elite-night credits or elite benefits by booking through a third-party portal. - The price and booking terms are competitive. If BofA Travel has the same or a better price than booking directly, using the portal can make sense — especially if you're also earning bonus rewards or redeeming points. When booking directly may be better Before booking, do a quick price check with the airline, hotel or rental car company directly. BofA Travel won't always have the lowest rate, and there's no reason to spend more just to book through the portal. Be especially careful with chain hotels. Because BofA Travel is a third-party booking platform, you'll give up hotel points, elite-night credits and elite benefits by booking through the portal. An independent hotel, on the other hand, is a safer bet since you won't be sacrificing those loyalty perks. Finally, check the change and cancellation terms before paying. As I found while testing the portal, these can vary significantly by booking. Some reservations were nonrefundable, and some flights had to be managed directly with the airline after booking. Earning rewards on BofA Travel bookings The rewards you'll earn on BofA Travel bookings depend on which Bank of America card you use: - Bank of America Travel Rewards credit card: Earn 3 points per dollar spent on purchases made through the Travel Center. - Bank of America Premium Rewards credit card: Earn 2 points per dollar spent on travel purchases. - Bank of America Premium Rewards Elite credit card: Earn 2 points per dollar spent on travel purchases. - Bank of America Customized Cash Rewards credit card: Earn 3% cash back on eligible travel purchases if travel is your selected choice category, on up to $2,500 in combined choice category, grocery store and wholesale club purchases each quarter (then 1%; this card offers 6% back on your choice category in the first cardholder year, up to the aforementioned quarterly maximum). - Bank of America Unlimited Cash Rewards credit card: Earn unlimited 1.5% cash back on purchases. BofA Rewards™ can make these rates even better. Depending on your tier, you can get a 10% to 75% rewards bonus on eligible Bank of America cards. Bottom line BofA Travel may not get as much attention as other credit card travel portals, but there's plenty to like about the revamped booking experience. It's especially useful for Premium Rewards Elite cardholders, who get a 20% points discount on airfare. Just compare prices and booking terms before you book to make sure BofA Travel is the best option for your trip.

item.title: This tiny airline lets you skip TSA and fly between small airports for less
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 4.64
This tiny airline lets you skip TSA and fly between small airports for less I had never before been to an airport where I could arrive 20 minutes before my flight, park for free, walk straight into the terminal and board a nine-seat plane without passing through the typical commercial airport security process. But that's exactly what happened when I flew SeaPort Airlines between Spokane, Washington, and Seattle this summer. What is SeaPort? "Please don't tell anyone about this," fellow passenger Ken Batali pleaded, moments after we disembarked a SeaPort Airlines Pilatus PC-12 turboprop plane, grabbed our bags off the cart and walked through a silent terminal to an empty curb. Along with five other passengers — more people than usual, according to our pilot — we had flown on one of SeaPort's fairly new scheduled flights between Felts Field (SFF) airport in Spokane, Washington, and King County International Airport - Boeing Field (BFI), just 5 miles south of downtown Seattle. Instead of flying from Seattle-Tacoma International Airport (SEA) to Spokane International Airport (GEG), SeaPort Airlines operates between smaller general aviation airports (which primarily serve private, corporate, charter and other non-major-airline flights); these airports are often much closer to city centers than their larger, commercial counterparts. So, no one had to show up more than 20 minutes before the Spokane-Seattle flight, pay for parking or pass through Transportation Security Administration-style security screening. There was no limit on liquids, and each passenger could bring up to 50 pounds of baggage, including a small pet in a carrier, for free. Batali, who lives about 30 miles north of Seattle, has been flying to Spokane regularly for work. He loves that the SeaPort flights from small airports save him time and hassle when compared to typical commercial flights. How do the prices compare? Batali said he noticed that trying to book a flight weeks in advance on SeaPort usually costs more than booking in advance on either Alaska Airlines or Delta Air Lines (which fly larger planes between the larger airports, SEA and GEG). When we compared commercial versus SeaPort prices, there was about a $50 difference. However, it's the last-minute bookings — a reality of business travel — where Seaport has made Batali's life much easier. "Booking last minute, as I usually do, I can always get a seat, and the ticket price is the same as last minute on Alaska," he said. If word about SeaPort gets out, he's worried it will be more difficult (and more expensive) to make a last-minute reservation on a nine-seat aircraft. And word does seem to be getting out. On our flight, a three-member finance team from a major Spokane company was testing the time and cost benefit of SeaPort's approximately one-hour, Spokane-to-Seattle flight between the two general aviation airports. "The ticket price was pretty much the same, we all had time to have dinner at home, we got free parking, and we'll have lower Uber fees in Seattle because we land closer to downtown," one team member told me. SeaPort Airlines — a Juneau, Alaska-based carrier — began offering scheduled flights between Seattle's Boeing Field and Spokane's Felts Field in March 2026. Flights between Boeing Field and the general aviation provider next to Portland International Airport (PDX) began in May 2025. (A previous incarnation of SeaPort served that route between 2008 and 2016). And this summer, SeaPort offered seasonal service to the general aviation terminal in Redmond, Oregon, near Redmond Municipal Airport (RDM). What was it like to fly SeaPort? In August, I became curious about this tiny airline whose tagline is: "It's about time." So, I took scheduled flights between all four Pacific Northwest cities that SeaPort Airlines serves. Out of habit, I showed up an hour before each flight, which I discovered was far too early since there's no metal detector, formal identification check or other security screening. All bags get weighed, but otherwise, the preflight experience consisted of the pilot and co-pilot greeting passengers in the waiting area, checking names against a list, walking the group out to the plane and loading the bags into a netted area at the rear of the plane. Walking the few steps from the terminal to the plane for the first flight, I stopped and took a step back. Not just because I wanted to snap a photo of the airplane, but because I realized it's been a very long time since I've flown in a small plane — and this Pilatus PC-12 turboprop plane looked very small. I followed my very calm-looking fellow passengers onto the plane and took a seat by the exit door. While not fancy, there was a definite private-jet feeling. The pilot swiveled around from the cockpit to give the safety briefing before takeoff. Like Batali and the finance team from the Spokane company that requested anonymity, my fellow passengers on each flight were mostly business travelers. On my flight from Redmond through Portland and home to Seattle, I met first-time passenger Brian Hayvaz. Hayvaz is the vice president of operations for Aircare International, a Tacoma, Washington-based company that provides emergency training for the crews that staff business and private jets. The SeaPort Airlines flight had popped up in his regular commercial flight search, and he'd booked a seat right away. "I assumed SeaPort was going to be too expensive, but the pricing was competitive. It's easy and convenient," Hayvaz said. "I'd fly this airline to other destinations if I could." In addition to company executives, Andy Kline, SeaPort Airlines' marketing manager, said the passenger makeup is proving a bit surprising. "We get electricians, roofers, project managers and contractors," Kline said. "It's a lot of people who need to get to job sites in other cities and a lot of people who charge by the hour." It's certainly a different, more convenient and often less expensive way to travel regionally. No security screening? The "no TSA-style security screening" aspect of SeaPort Airlines' service is, for some, one of the more appealing and intriguing aspects of the flight experience. Airline staff watches for hazardous materials and issues, such as passengers who may be unfit for travel, Kline said. He also added that relaxed security screening is allowed because the airline is a Part 135 carrier under Federal Aviation Administration regulations, which govern scheduled service carriers operating planes carrying nine or fewer passengers, with some exceptions. But as Hansford Smith, vice president of risk management at Silver Air Private Jets, noted: "The absence of a traditional checkpoint does not mean there is no security screening." There are a variety of reasons why TSA-type screening may or may not apply to passengers on flights operated by other Part 135 operators offering scheduled service, such as Cape Air, JSX, Boutique Air, Tradewind Aviation, Mokulele Airlines and Kenmore Airlines. "In many, if not most, instances, it is a case-by-case determination by the TSA as to what the required security protocols will be," Mark A. Dombroff, partner and aviation attorney at Fox Rothschild LLP, said. He notes that the determining factors may range from the airports involved and whether passengers board or deplane through the sterile or secure areas of the airport, to the maximum certificated weight and seating capacity of the aircraft.

item.title: 7 ways I'd redeem the 125,000-mile bonus on the Citi / AAdvantage Executive card
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 4.37
7 ways I'd redeem the 125,000-mile bonus on the Citi / AAdvantage Executive card Editor's Note American Airlines AAdvantage miles offer excellent value, particularly for lie-flat business-class seats and the occasional first-class flight. With the welcome bonus on the Citi® / AAdvantage® Executive World Legend Mastercard® (see rates and fees), you have enough miles to chase some genuinely premium redemptions. Right now, there's a limited-time, best-ever bonus: Earn 125,000 bonus miles after spending $15,000 on purchases in the first five months from account opening. Based on TPG's September 2026 valuations, this bonus alone is worth $1,813. But here's a sweetener: Combine that 125,000-mile bonus with the miles you'll earn on the $15,000 minimum spending requirement (at least 1 mile per dollar), and you're looking at a minimum of 140,000 AAdvantage miles to redeem. The AAdvantage program has both a fixed award chart for most partners and dynamic pricing (which can fluctuate based on demand) for American Airlines and Fiji Airways flights. In this guide, I focus primarily on fixed-price redemptions with partner airlines, as they offer predictable value (though you'll also find some American Airlines and Fiji Airways options). I've used over a million AAdvantage miles to fly to places like Brazil, Hong Kong and Jordan, so here are my top seven picks for redemptions that deliver real value. Business class to Europe Transatlantic business class is one of the most prized redemptions for those with points and miles. You have solid options for American's own Flagship cabin and on partner carriers, each with distinct advantages. American Airlines I flew American's newest business-class seat between Chicago's O'Hare International Airport (ORD) and London's Heathrow Airport (LHR) last summer, and while I don't think it's a world-leading product, it's definitely a step above the older seat. The sliding privacy door is ideal for sleeping on the red-eye flight to Europe. This redemption is priced dynamically. The cheapest I found from ORD to LHR over the next year was 73,500 miles (plus $5.60 in taxes and fees), with a more common price of 97,000 to 100,000 miles. Finnair and Iberia Finnair operates nonstop to Helsinki Airport (HEL) — ideally placed for Nordic exploration and connections throughout Europe — from: - Dallas Fort Worth International Airport (DFW) - Miami International Airport (MIA) - New York's John F. Kennedy International Airport (JFK) - ORD - Seattle-Tacoma International Airport (SEA) The carrier's Airbus A350 business-class cabin is comfortable, with excellent food and friendly service. Both Finnair and Iberia offer fixed-price redemptions at 57,500 miles one-way (plus $5.60 in taxes and fees), and you can connect throughout Europe on the same award without burning extra Avios (just pay the applicable taxes). I'm based in Madrid (Iberia's hub) and can confirm it offers strong availability and solid access across the U.S. Avoid British Airways Here's where British Airways stands apart from American Airlines, Finnair and Iberia: It adds fuel surcharges onto award redemptions. An ORD-to-LHR flight on American costs $5.60. Fly the same route on British Airways, and you're looking at $734. That's a huge gap. Qsuite to the Middle East and beyond I've flown Qatar Airways' Qsuite several times, and I'm flying it again at the end of the year to Australia to visit family. This product set the gold standard for business-class design. If traveling with a companion, you can convert two adjacent suites into a double bed. You can fly from most major U.S. airports to Doha's Hamad International Airport (DOH) for 70,000 miles (plus $15 in taxes and fees). Connections to the Middle East, Egypt, India or the Maldives cost no additional miles (just taxes), and onward flights to Africa add 5,000 miles. Award availability for these flights can be tight, so use a tool like Thrifty Traveler or Seats.aero for alerts. Qatar Airways delivers excellent service and food, with Starlink high-speed Wi-Fi on most long-haul flights. Flights from U.S. airports to DOH take 13 to 17 hours, so you can make that time genuinely productive. First class to Asia Cathay Pacific and Japan Airlines are both high-quality Oneworld partners that offer access to first-class travel across the Pacific. AAdvantage gives you access to two distinct products, each with its own appeal. Fly to Tokyo's Haneda Airport (HND) on Japan Airlines for 80,000 miles one-way (plus $5.60 in taxes and fees) in its latest Airbus A350 first class, which operates from DFW, JFK and Los Angeles International Airport (LAX). The airline excels in food and service and features embedded seat speakers for a more immersive experience. This is one of the next redemptions I'm eyeing. Or, you can fly Cathay Pacific first class one-way to Hong Kong International Airport (HKG) for 110,000 miles (plus $5.60 in taxes and fees), with business-class connections throughout Asia included (taxes only). The onboard product feels dated, but you'll get excellent food and access to the newly renovated The Wing, First lounge at HKG, which features private shower suites, fine dining and spa services. Business class to the South Pacific Australia and New Zealand are far away, so premium cabins make sense. Qantas to Australia and New Zealand Flying Qantas, Australia's flag carrier, Down Under costs 80,000 miles one-way in business class (plus $28 in taxes and fees). The airline flies from several U.S. airports to Australia's Sydney Airport (SYD), Melbourne Airport (MEL) and Brisbane Airport (BNE) and also operates from JFK to Auckland Airport (AKL) in New Zealand. I'll be honest: In my experience, it's an average product in terms of customer service, food and the seat itself. But beggars can't be choosers when flying premium cabins across the Pacific. Business-class awards on transpacific flights are among the most coveted redemptions available, so book either 11 months before departure (when the AAdvantage calendar opens) or within a month before departure (when remaining seats are released). Fiji Airways Fiji Airways has dynamic pricing starting at 80,000 miles one-way (plus $5.60 in taxes and fees) to Fiji's Nadi International Airport (NAN). The airline operates from DFW, LAX and San Francisco International Airport (SFO), and Fiji has become an increasingly popular stop on longer South Pacific itineraries. Fiji Airways is known for its warm service and child-friendly environment. Business class to Morocco Royal Air Maroc has reliable award availability for lie-flat business-class seats from JFK, LAX, MIA and Dulles International Airport (IAD) near Washington, D.C., to Mohammed V International Airport (CMN) in Casablanca, Morocco. The product isn't luxurious, but it offers good value at 57,500 miles (plus $5.60 in taxes and fees). You can connect onward through Morocco for no additional miles (taxes only) or catch the high-speed rail to Marrakech in about three hours. More broadly, the airline operates extensive service across Southern and Western Europe, so Casablanca serves as a good connecting hub even if Morocco isn't your destination. Short-haul domestic flights in economy Not every trip calls for premium cabins. Cash fares for domestic flights have increased significantly, so redeeming AAdvantage miles and paying as little as $5.60 in taxes and fees can offer good value. Short-haul economy flights, such as those from Austin-Bergstrom International Airport (AUS) to DFW, start at just 5,000 miles. Use economy awards strategically on routes where other airlines don't compete effectively. Select flights from airports outside the US The best miles value sometimes comes from redemptions booked outside the U.S., especially if you're already traveling internationally and can position yourself at the right hub. - Australia to Southeast Asia: I'm flying from SYD to Ninoy Aquino International Airport (MNL) in the Philippines in January, with the eight-hour Qantas business-class flight costing me only 40,000 miles (plus $80 in taxes and fees). - Etihad Airways first class between Europe and the Middle East: I've flown this product once before, and you can take a shower in the sky. A sweet spot is flying from its hub at Abu Dhabi's Zayed International Airport (AUH) to Paris-Charles de Gaulle Airport (CDG) or LHR for 62,500 miles (plus $37 in taxes and fees). If you can find award availability, it's one of the most aspirational redemptions in the world. - Gol Airlines within South America: Using cash for domestic flights within Brazil can be expensive. But you can redeem AAdvantage miles on Gol Airlines flights within Brazil (except Manaus) for 7,000 miles one-way (plus $7 in taxes and fees) and from Brazil to Argentina for 10,000 miles (plus $13 in taxes and fees). It's one of the region's best-value redemption options. Bottom line The 125,000-mile welcome bonus on the Citi / AAdvantage Executive World Legend Mastercard is substantial, although the $15,000 spending requirement won't make sense for everyone. If you can meet it without spending more than you normally would, you'll end up with at least 140,000 AAdvantage miles. That's enough for two one-way business-class awards to Europe, a round-trip Qsuite itinerary to the Maldives or a one-way first-class flight to Asia (assuming you can find availability). For me, AAdvantage miles remain most valuable for these fixed-price partner awards, particularly when the taxes and fees are low (as is the case for all of the recommendations in this guide). To learn more, read our full review of the Citi / AAdvantage Executive card. Apply here: Citi / AAdvantage Executive World Legend Mastercard

item.title: Frontier Airlines to end service at New York's JFK after 2-year run
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 4.09
Frontier Airlines to end service at New York's JFK after 2-year run New York City's biggest airport is losing service from one of the top budget airlines in the U.S. Frontier Airlines plans to wind down all operations at John F. Kennedy International Airport (JFK) in early October. Flights will officially end on Oct. 5, a spokesperson for the airline confirmed Friday. It's time to book: When to buy holiday, spring break and summer flights for the best fares in 2026-27 The move doesn't come as a major shock. Earlier this year, Frontier cut most of its flights at JFK, keeping only its Atlanta route. Now, the carrier also plans to end that daily service to Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport (ATL). In a statement, Frontier pointed to a handful of factors — including the high costs of operating at JFK. "We periodically review and update routes based on market demand, seasonality, costs associated with operating from a particular airport, and other factors," the carrier said. A 2-year run at JFK In the end, Frontier lasted a little more than two years at JFK. The Denver-based, ultra-low-cost carrier launched service from the airport in June 2024 while in the midst of a major network shake-up. At the time, it was a bit of a gamble and a left turn, of sorts, for the airline, opting to operate at an airport that's one of the nation's most premium markets for long-haul international travel. As recently as last summer, the discounter served eight nonstop destinations from JFK — and had announced plans to operate from the airport's new Terminal 6, which is currently under construction. It appears that's now unlikely to happen. Frontier will stay at LaGuardia, Newark Frontier does still have a presence at the other two major hubs in the New York City area. The carrier serves four destinations from LaGuardia Airport (LGA): ATL, Dallas Fort Worth International Airport (DFW), Charlotte Douglas International Airport (CLT) and Orlando International Airport (MCO). It also offers ATL, DFW and MCO flights from nearby Newark Liberty International Airport (EWR). Worth noting: Frontier's old foe, Spirit Airlines, had been the No. 2 airline at Newark before its collapse. So far, Frontier hasn't made a major push to backfill EWR routes abandoned by Spirit. The airline's CEO, James Dempsey, has advocated a more methodical route-planning approach in the wake of its former rival's demise. "We'll be cherry-picking what we think is the right path and market to go into the future," he told me in July, speaking about the airline's broader strategy. "But there will be some former Spirit routes that we look at." Read more: Frontier wants to be an airline you'd choose to fly. Will first class and new perks do the trick? Looking ahead Frontier did leave the door open to a potential return to JFK down the road. "As with any station closure," a spokesperson said. "[We] will evaluate market conditions going forward to consider a return at some point in the future." Related reading:

item.title: Delta cuts 5 routes across 7 cities, plans smaller Las Vegas schedule this winter
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 4.09
Delta cuts 5 routes across 7 cities, plans smaller Las Vegas schedule this winter As the peak summer travel season wrapped up this past weekend, Delta Air Lines revealed plans to slash five routes from its network. Between now and December, Delta plans to trim a total of three routes from New York City: two from John F. Kennedy International Airport (JFK) and one from LaGuardia Airport (LGA). The Atlanta-based carrier will also end Las Vegas service from two cities in Southern California. It's time to book: When to buy holiday, spring break and summer flights for the best fares in 2026-27 That cutback at Harry Reid International Airport (LAS) came as a result of lower travel demand to Vegas this winter, a spokesperson said. Meanwhile, here's how the airline explained its cuts in New York City: "Delta continually evaluates its network to ensure we're offering a schedule that best meets customer demand," the airline said in a statement about the changes. "We apologize for any inconvenience and will contact impacted customers directly about these changes." Delta's 5 route cuts All five of the routes will end between early November and mid-December. Here's the full rundown of the flights Delta is ending: | Route | End date | |---|---| | LAS to San Diego International Airport (SAN) | Nov. 8 | | LAS to John Wayne Airport (SNA) in Orange County, California | Nov. 8 | | LGA to Tulsa International Airport (TUL) | Nov. 9 | | JFK to Palm Springs International Airport (PSP) | Saturday-only service ends Dec. 19 | | JFK to Milwaukee Mitchell International Airport (MKE) | Dec. 19 | There is a silver lining for Delta flyers in New York and Wisconsin who have taken the JFK-MKE service in the past: The carrier still offers four daily round-trip flights between LGA and MKE. And, Delta does plan to operate some limited Las Vegas service to both San Diego and Orange County in early January. Those flights are meant to cater to travelers attending the city's massive Consumer Electronics Show, where the airline has been a headliner in the past. Cutting back in Las Vegas Delta is not alone in cutting back its Vegas flight schedule. This winter, the airline's total departures from LAS will be down roughly 7% versus last year, according to data from aviation analytics firm Cirium. In 2026, the entire airport is set to see 7% fewer flights than last year, per Cirium. That's after the city as a whole saw a 7.5% dropoff in visitors last year versus 2024, according to the Las Vegas Convention and Visitors Bureau. It came amid one of the "more complex operating environments" the tourism sector had seen outside of the COVID-19 pandemic, the organization said in January. Related reading:

item.title: Is the Citi / AAdvantage Executive World Legend Mastercard worth it?
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 4.05
Is the Citi / AAdvantage Executive World Legend Mastercard worth it? Editor's Note If you fly American Airlines frequently, you may want to consider getting one of its cobranded Citi cards. At the top of the hierarchy is the Citi® / AAdvantage® Executive World Legend Mastercard® (see rates and fees), which offers the most AA-specific perks of any credit card. The card recently underwent a significant refresh in August, which raised the annual fee to $695 but also added substantial new benefits. Doing the math on this card is now more important than ever — but there's also more value to potentially unlock if you maximize each of the new perks. So, is it worth the annual fee — both in year one and beyond? Let's do the math. Welcome bonus New Citi / AAdvantage Executive World Legend Mastercard cardholders can currently earn a limited time offer of 125,000 bonus miles after spending $15,000 on purchases in the first five months from account opening. This bonus is worth about $1,813, based on TPG's September 2026 valuations, and is the highest we've seen on the card, so now is the best time to apply. This bonus accounts for a significant portion of the card's overall value, so earning it and redeeming the miles wisely are crucial to offsetting the card's high annual fee. Related: The Citi / AAdvantage Executive's new benefits are live: 6 things to do now Lounge access Arguably, the most valuable ongoing benefit of this card is the complimentary Admirals Club membership you'll receive every year that you hold it. When you have the Citi / AA Executive, all you have to do is walk to the lounge and present a same-day boarding pass for an eligible flight. An annual membership costs $750 to $1,400, depending on your status level and whether you want access only to AA-branded lounges or to partner lounges as well. Given that this card carries a $695 annual fee, it doesn't make sense to buy an Admirals Club membership on its own, unless you aren't eligible for the card. With this card, you'll be able to access almost 50 Admirals Clubs and more than 60 partner lounges worldwide when flying American or one of its Oneworld partners. Notably, this includes Alaska Lounges in hubs like Los Angeles International Airport (LAX), Portland International Airport (PDX), San Francisco International Airport (SFO) and Seattle-Tacoma International Airport (SEA). You can bring in either your immediate family members (spouse or domestic partner and children under 18 years of age) or up to two guests. And they don't need to be on the same flight as you — just any American or Oneworld flight with a same-day boarding pass. Related: The best lounge access credit cards to add to your wallet Travel benefits The Citi / AA Executive offers valuable perks when flying American, including priority check-in at business-class counters (where available) and priority boarding privileges (where available) for you and up to eight travelers on the same reservation. You also get your first checked bag free on domestic itineraries with American Airlines, saving you at least $45 each time. (Note that this is only for domestic flights; I had to pay out of pocket when I traveled to Mexico, forgetting the restrictions of this perk.) Additionally, you'll receive a statement credit of up to $120 for Global Entry/TSA PreCheck. (I suggest maximizing your credit by applying for Global Entry, as it includes PreCheck anyway.) You'll also receive elite status with two partner programs: - Omni Champion, which includes room upgrades, early check-in and late checkout privileges (subject to availability), and an annual free night reward after qualifying stays at participating Omni Hotels properties. - Avis President's Club (through Aug. 31, 2028), providing car rental upgrades (subject to availability), the ability to skip the rental counter at major airports and complimentary additional drivers. Furthermore, the card includes travel protections, such as trip cancellation, trip interruption, trip delay, lost baggage protection and car rental insurance coverage. And there are no foreign transaction fees, making this card a good option for international purchases. Related: Which airline is now best if you don't want to pay bag fees? Elite status If chasing AAdvantage elite status is important to you, the Citi / AA Executive will help you achieve it. You'll earn 1 Loyalty Point for every mile you earn from purchases. Cardholders also earn 10,000 bonus Loyalty Points after reaching each of the following milestones in the same status qualification year: - 50,000 Loyalty Points - 90,000 Loyalty Points - 165,000 Loyalty Points - 240,000 Loyalty Points Related: 8 methods that earned American AAdvantage Executive Platinum Statement credits The statement credits on the Citi / AA Executive include: - Up to $500 in annual American Airlines Vacations statement credits (up to $250 every six months) - Up to $180 in annual Lyft credits ($15 monthly) — but you have to take three eligible rides each month first to receive this credit - Up to $120 back in statement credits on eligible prepaid rentals booked directly on Avis.com or Budget.com every calendar year - Up to $100 annual statement credit for eligible American Airlines inflight and Admirals Club purchases The American Airlines Vacations credits are only valuable if you'd book these packages anyway. Note that the credit splits into two $250 six-month periods — you must use one in the first half of the year and one in the second; unused credits don't roll over. Qualifying packages typically require at least two travel components (flight plus hotel, flight plus rental car, etc.), though you can often minimize costs by adding a cheap rental car to a flight or hotel booking. I've had issues with the car rental credit, so I wouldn't rely on it for value. Previously, a Budget rental in Cabo was not coded correctly, and Citi wouldn't manually apply the credit. Later, I completed another Budget rental in Ireland and waited the obligatory 10 weeks. Again, it didn't post, and again, Citi refused to apply a manual credit. I don't value the Lyft perk because you don't get the $15 credit until after you've taken three (non-discounted) rides in a month. Instead, I use my Chase Sapphire Reserve® (see rates and fees) to earn 5 points per dollar spent, plus a $10 monthly in-app credit on Lyft purchases (through Sept. 30, 2027). The inflight (and Admirals Club) credit is useful if you regularly buy onboard refreshments or snacks. Related: Frequent Uber or Lyft user? These are the best credit cards for you Earning and redeeming miles If you're looking to supercharge your points earning across several programs, I'd suggest putting your spending on a card that earns transferable points. However, if you want to maximize your AAdvantage mile balance specifically, the Citi / AA Executive will earn you: - 12 miles per dollar spent on eligible car rentals and hotels booked through American's car rental and hotel booking sites, respectively - 4 miles per dollar spent on eligible American Airlines purchases (jumps to 5 miles per dollar spent for the remainder of the calendar year once you've spent $150,000 on purchases in a calendar year) - 1 mile per dollar spent on all other eligible purchases AAdvantage miles are more valuable (at 1.45 cents each) than United MileagePlus miles (1.2 cents) and Delta SkyMiles (1.2 cents), according to our valuations. I redeemed part of the welcome bonus I received on this card for a luxurious flight. I used 70,000 miles plus $174 for a one-way business-class flight in Qatar Airways' fantastic Qsuite from Doha to Houston. Given that this flight retails for $3,910 one-way, I got a very high 5.6 cents per mile from this redemption, quadruple TPG's valuation of AAdvantage miles. Related: The best uses of American Airlines AAdvantage miles Authorized users Finally, the Citi / AA Executive is a great option if you want to extend Admirals Club access to friends and family affordably. You can add up to three authorized users for $175 total (about $58 each), and $175 each after that. Each authorized user receives Admirals Club access (with a same-day boarding pass for an eligible flight) for themselves and up to two traveling companions. However, authorized users only get Admirals Club access, not a full Admirals Club membership. Related: Everything you need to know about authorized credit card users Bottom line Ultimately, if you value Admirals Club access, priority perks on American flights and a large welcome bonus, this card can easily justify its fee. You'll get even more value if you take advantage of its statement credits and authorized user perks. But if lounge access isn't important to you, consider one of Citi's lower-fee AAdvantage cards instead. To learn more, read our full review of the Citi / AA Executive World Legend Mastercard. Apply here: Citi / AAdvantage Executive World Legend Mastercard TPG featured card | 4X | Earn 4X Membership Rewards® points per dollar spent on purchases at restaurants worldwide, on up to $50,000 in purchases per calendar year, then 1X points for the rest of the year. | | 4X | Earn 4X Membership Rewards® points per dollar spent at US supermarkets, on up to $25,000 in purchases per calendar year, then 1X points for the rest of the year. | | 5X | Earn 5X Membership Rewards® points on prepaid hotel stays booked through AmexTravel.com or the Amex Travel App™. | | 3X | Earn 3X Membership Rewards® points on flights booked through AmexTravel.com, the Amex Travel App™, or purchased directly from airlines. | | 2X | Earn 2X Membership Rewards® points on prepaid car rentals booked through AmexTravel.com or the Amex Travel App™ and cruises booked and paid through AmexTravel.com. | | 1X | Earn 1X Membership Rewards® point per dollar spent on all other eligible purchases. |

item.title: Ultimate guide to Frontier Miles: How to earn and redeem miles, elite status and more
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 3.76
Ultimate guide to Frontier Miles: How to earn and redeem miles, elite status and more Editor's Note With its discount fares and robust frequent flyer program, Frontier Miles can offer great value for frequent Frontier Airlines travelers. As a Frontier Miles member, you can earn miles and elite status. Frontier elite status offers multiple perks to make your travels more enjoyable and less expensive, including complimentary luggage, priority boarding and the ability to pool your miles. You can then redeem your miles for award travel. Here's an overview of how the program works. How to earn Frontier points and miles The Frontier Miles program is free to join. It offers two types of rewards: miles redeemable for award flights and elite status points used to reach elite status tiers and get perks like free bags and seat selection. Earn points and miles on eligible Frontier purchases Under its revenue-based mileage accrual system, Frontier Miles allows you to earn based on the dollar amount of your ticket plus any additional products you purchase. For bookings made on or after Sept. 1, how many miles and elite status points you earn depends on your elite status, whether you purchase a basic fare or an Economy, Premium or Business bundle and whether you're a Frontier Airlines World Mastercard® holder. Bundled fares now earn significantly more than basic fares. The information for the Frontier Airlines World Mastercard has been collected independently by The Points Guy. The card details on this page have not been reviewed or provided by the card issuer. Here are Frontier's current earning rates: | Tier | 2026 qualification | Basic fare | Basic fare, cardmember | Economy, Premium or Business bundle | Economy, Premium or Business bundle, cardmember | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | Member (no status) | After enrollment | 1 mile and 1 point per dollar spent | 4 miles and 4 points per dollar spent | 6 miles and 6 points per dollar spent | 12 miles and 12 points per dollar spent | | Elite Silver | 10,000 points | 3 miles and 3 points per dollar spent | 6 miles and 6 points per dollar spent | 8 miles and 8 points per dollar spent | 14 miles and 14 points per dollar spent | | Elite Gold | 20,000 points | 5 miles and 5 points per dollar spent | 8 miles and 8 points per dollar spent | 10 miles and 10 points per dollar spent | 16 miles and 16 points per dollar spent | | Elite Platinum | 50,000 points | 7 miles and 7 points per dollar spent | 10 miles and 10 points per dollar spent | 12 miles and 12 points per dollar spent | 18 miles and 18 points per dollar spent | | Elite Diamond | 75,000 points | 11 miles and 11 points per dollar spent | 14 miles and 14 points per dollar spent | 16 miles and 16 points per dollar spent | 22 miles and 22 points per dollar spent | These rates apply to bookings made on or after Sept. 1. Additionally, select Frontier Airlines World Mastercard holders who use their card for eligible Frontier purchases can earn an additional 5 miles and 1 elite status point per dollar spent. Earn redeemable miles and elite status points with the Frontier Airlines credit card Frontier Airlines partners with Barclays to offer the Frontier Airlines World Mastercard. New cardmembers earn 60,000 bonus miles: 50,000 miles after spending $500 on purchases and paying the annual fee in full in the first 90 days from account opening, plus 10,000 miles after adding an authorized user who makes a purchase in the first 90 days. You can also unlock Elite Gold status for 90 days after making your first purchase in the first 90 days of account opening. You can retain Elite Gold status for 12 months from account opening by spending $3,000 in the first 90 days. The card earns 5 miles per dollar spent on eligible Frontier purchases, 3 miles per dollar spent at restaurants and 1 mile per dollar spent on other purchases. You'll also earn 1 elite status point for every dollar spent on the card. The card offers valuable benefits like Group 4 boarding on all Frontier flights, two free checked bags and family miles pooling. You can also earn a $100 flight voucher each account anniversary after spending $2,500 or more on purchases with your card during the card membership year. Unless you place a high value on Frontier Airlines miles and elite status, we generally don't recommend this card. Most travelers are better off with a transferable points or miles credit card like the Chase Sapphire Preferred® Card (see rates and fees). Earn miles with Frontier's partners Frontier offers several more ways to earn miles, but keep in mind that these only earn miles, not points toward elite status. Frontier has relationships with several major rental car companies, so you can earn bonus miles and access negotiated rates when booking through Frontier's partner page. While earning rates depend on the rental car company, you can generally earn between 50 and 100 miles per rental, per day or between 500 and 1,000 miles per rental. Frontier Miles also partners with Marriott Bonvoy and Wyndham Rewards. Marriott Bonvoy members can earn 1 to 2 Frontier miles per dollar spent at participating Marriott brands, and Wyndham Rewards members can also earn 1 to 2 Frontier miles per dollar spent at participating hotels, depending on their status. In both cases, you must update your hotel loyalty account preferences to earn Frontier miles instead of hotel points. We don't recommend doing this since you'll typically get a lower return with Frontier miles. For example, basic Bonvoy members earn 10 points per dollar spent at Autograph Collection hotels. According to TPG's September 2026 valuations, which put Bonvoy points at 0.75 cents each, that's a return of 7.5%. Compare that to the 2 Frontier miles per dollar you would earn at Autograph Collection hotels, which provides only a 2.6% return. You also have the option to convert your existing hotel points to Frontier miles. Marriott points transfer to Frontier at a 3:1 ratio, while Wyndham points transfer to Frontier at a 5:1 ratio. Frontier also became a transfer partner of Rove in July 2026. Rove miles transfer to Frontier Miles at a 1:1 ratio, giving members another way to top off a Frontier account without flying or using the Frontier credit card. Frontier has a few other partners to give you more options for earning miles. You can earn 10 miles per dollar spent when you order flowers from Teleflora. Or, you can book a cruise through Frontier Cruises and earn miles at a preset rate: - One- to five-night cruises: 1,500 miles - Six- to eight-night cruises: 3,000 miles - Nine- to 12-night cruises: 5,000 miles - Cruises 13 nights and longer: 10,000 miles This may be a useful option for Frontier loyalists, but you can often earn more miles by booking through other cruise platforms. Lastly, you can buy Frontier miles at 2.5 cents per mile. This is considerably higher than TPG's September 2026 valuation of 1.3 cents per Frontier mile, so we don't advise it in most cases. However, if you're planning a redemption and you're short a few miles, it could make sense. Related: When does it make sense to buy points and miles? How to redeem Frontier miles One-way award flights currently start at the following rates: - Basic: From 5,000 miles - Economy: From 7,000 miles - Premium: From 9,000 miles - Business: From 13,000 miles Frontier says there are no blackout dates for award flights, although the number of miles required varies by flight and availability. Taxes and fees start at $5.60 each way but can increase sharply depending on the destination. | Destination | One-way taxes and fees from | Round-trip taxes and fees from | |---|---|---| | U.S. and Puerto Rico | $5.60 | $11.20 | | Mexico | $40.71 | $126.24 | | Dominican Republic | $46.90 to $49.65 | $115.55 to $121.05 | | Jamaica | $49.60 | $142.42 to $168.70 | | El Salvador | $7.10 | $63.58 | | Bahamas | $6.60 | $116.65 | | Costa Rica | $22.68 to $22.95 | $77.04 to $83.62 | | Guatemala | $5.60 | $55.50 | | Antigua | $43.10 | $97.95 | Redeem miles for add-ons Economy bundles start at just 2,000 miles. If you want to use miles for a bundle, you must select the "Use miles for bundles" option before choosing your flight during the original booking process. Frontier allows bundles to be paired with standard, Discount Den, GoWild and award fares. Considering Frontier provides many add-on options — and has various fees that can quickly stack up, even if you book your ticket with miles — being able to redeem miles for these items could be a great asset for Frontier Miles members. Redeeming your 5,000-mile Super Bowl weekend bonus If you were lucky enough to catch Frontier's Super Bowl weekend promotion (no longer available), you might be wondering how you can use your 5,000 miles. Fortunately, basic award flights now start at 5,000 miles one-way, meaning you can use your entire bonus in one go. For example, you could fly between Denver International Airport (DEN) and Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport (ATL) for just 5,000 miles one-way, plus $6 in taxes and fees. These great deals can be found on longer journeys and even on connecting flights. Flights from San Francisco International Airport (SFO) to Tampa International Airport (TPA) via DEN start from the same 5,000 miles plus $6 in taxes and fees. With this Super Bowl weekend bonus in hand, you'd have enough miles to book either of these redemptions. Frontier's Discount Den membership Frontier Airlines offers a membership program called Discount Den. While not the same as elite status, this program provides access to discounted fares for a $59.99 annual membership fee. New members must also pay a $50 enrollment fee, bringing the first-year cost to $109.99. On "Kids Fly Free" flights, one child under 15 can fly free for every adult Discount Den fare purchased, offering excellent savings on certain routes. We've historically found that Discount Den can offer pretty good deals, too, with savings of $20 per person on both domestic and international tickets. Discount Den can also help you earn Frontier status. The purchase of the Discount Den membership itself earns Frontier miles and elite status points at Frontier's bundle earning rate. We recommend that frequent Frontier flyers consider a Discount Den membership if they expect to save more than $109.99 in their first membership year or more than $59.99 in subsequent years. It's easier to get value from a Discount Den membership when you travel with kids; a family of four may recoup the annual cost with just one family vacation. Frontier's GoWild Pass Frontier Airlines also offers an all-you-can-fly pass called GoWild. Frontier regularly changes the types and prices of GoWild passes it sells. As of September 2026, the carrier is selling its fall and winter pass for $249, which covers travel through Feb. 28, 2027. GoWild flights can be confirmed the day before departure for domestic travel and beginning 10 days before departure for international travel. Frontier sometimes lets members book earlier on select flights for an additional early booking charge. Each flight segment has a fare of 1 cent, but government and airport taxes and fees still apply. You may find unexpectedly high fees and limited availability with this pass, depending on your travel dates and routes. Bags and seat assignments generally cost extra unless your elite status provides them. GoWild can also help you earn elite status. Eligible GoWild ticket purchases earn Frontier miles and elite status points, while the purchase of the GoWild Pass itself earns miles and elite status points at Frontier's bundle earning rates. Related: I bought a Frontier all-you-can-fly pass — here's what it was like to use it Frontier elite status Frontier announced significant changes to its elite status levels in August 2026. Elite Diamond status now requires just 75,000 elite status points, down from 100,000. For the remainder of 2026, Elite Silver status continues to require 10,000 points, Elite Gold status requires 20,000 points and Elite Platinum status requires 50,000 points. Beginning Jan. 1, 2027, the thresholds for Elite Silver and Elite Gold will increase to 15,000 and 25,000 points, respectively, while Elite Platinum and Elite Diamond will require 50,000 and 75,000 points, respectively. When you qualify for Frontier elite status during a calendar year, you can use that status for the remainder of the year in which you qualify and throughout the following calendar year. For example, if you reach an elite status tier in June 2026, you can enjoy that status through Dec. 31, 2027. However, your elite status point balance resets to zero at the beginning of each calendar year for requalification purposes, so you'll need to earn enough points each year to retain or improve your status. The following benefits apply to bookings made through Dec. 31, 2026. Elite Silver status: - No change/cancellation fees (more than seven days before departure) - Priority customer care - Family miles pooling - Standard seat at booking - Preferred seat at check-in - Group 4 boarding (for everyone on booking) Elite Gold status (includes the same benefits as Elite Silver, plus): - Carry-on bag (for only the member) - Preferred seat at booking - Premium seat at check-in - UpFront Plus (four hours before departure) - Group 1 boarding Elite Platinum status (includes the same benefits as Elite Gold, plus): - Carry-on bag (for everyone on booking) - First checked bag (for everyone on booking) - Standard seat at booking (for everyone on booking) - Premium or preferred seat at booking (for the member) - Premium or preferred seat at check-in (for everyone on booking) - UpFront Plus (12 hours before departure) - Group 1 boarding (for everyone on booking) - Companion travel - Pet-in-cabin fee waiver - 50% off Discount Den membership - Ability to gift Elite Silver status Elite Diamond status (includes the same benefits as Elite Platinum, plus): - Refundability (more than one day before departure) - Two checked bags (for everyone on booking) - Premium seat at booking (for everyone on booking) - UpFront Plus (upon check-in, subject to availability) - Priority boarding (for everyone on booking) - Discount Den membership - Ability to gift Elite Gold status Frontier elite status benefits from 2027 Frontier's new elite qualification thresholds take effect Jan. 1, 2027, while the updated elite benefits below apply to bookings made on or after Jan. 1, 2027. Each tier includes the benefits of the tiers below it. Elite Silver, at 15,000 points, will receive complimentary space-available upgrades to UpFront Plus or first class four hours before departure when traveling on an Economy or Premium bundle. Elite Silver members who buy an Economy bundle will also be eligible for upgrades to preferred seating, Group 4 boarding, priority customer care and family pooling. Elite Gold, at 25,000 points, will receive UpFront Plus or first-class upgrades eight hours before departure and premium seat upgrades when purchasing an Economy bundle. Elite Gold also includes a free carry-on bag and Group 1 boarding. Elite Platinum, at 50,000 points, will receive UpFront Plus or first-class upgrades 18 hours before departure and premium seat upgrades for everyone on the reservation when purchasing an Economy bundle. Elite Platinum will also include a free carry-on bag and one checked bag weighing up to 50 pounds for everyone on the booking, plus a waiver of the pet-in-cabin fee. However, the Elite Platinum tier's current unlimited companion travel benefit will be replaced by two companion travel certificates in 2027.
