Elite Diamond, at 75,000 points, will receive UpFront Plus or first-class upgrades 24 hours before departure, two checked bags weighing up to 50 pounds each for everyone on the reservation, unlimited companion travel and preboarding. Frontier also plans to introduce milestone rewards in 2027. These will let elite members select additional benefits as they progress through the program. The airline has not yet announced the full details. Ways to fast-track Frontier status You don't necessarily have to earn Frontier status solely by buying flights. A few shortcuts can help: - Use the Frontier Airlines World Mastercard: You'll earn 1 elite status point per dollar spent on card purchases, plus enhanced earnings on eligible Frontier bookings. Some card offers may also include a temporary shortcut to Elite Gold status, so check the current application terms. - Buy a Discount Den or GoWild Pass: Frontier treats the purchase price of both memberships as eligible spending that earns miles and elite status points at the applicable bundle rate. - Watch for status matches and promotions: Frontier has offered paid instant-status deals and status matches in the past, so it's worth keeping an eye on its status-match website for new opportunities. Bottom line The Frontier Miles loyalty program can be worthwhile for those who fly the airline often. Award flights start at just 5,000 miles, and members can now redeem miles for bundles starting at 2,000 miles, which can help offset some of the extra costs associated with flying an ultra-low-cost carrier. However, the program became much less rewarding for travelers who book basic fares without a Frontier credit card in September 2026, though its elite status can still be particularly valuable for families and travelers who want to avoid baggage and seat assignment fees. Whether Frontier Miles is worth pursuing ultimately depends on how well Frontier's route network and ultra-low-cost model fit your travel patterns. Status, the cobranded card and memberships like Discount Den can substantially reduce Frontier's add-on costs, but they don't change the carrier's more bare-bones basic fare experience or make sense if you rarely fly Frontier.

item.title: The 10 best places to travel in October 2026
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 3.44
The 10 best places to travel in October 2026 Editor's Note October is one of the best months to plan a leisure trip. In many popular destinations, it's shoulder season, bringing fewer crowds, lower hotel rates and comfortable weather. In the Northern Hemisphere, it's also prime time for fall foliage, while destinations south of the equator are welcoming spring with blooming flowers and warming temperatures. From leaf-peeping in New England to wine tasting in Vienna and chasing hot air balloons in Japan, these are 10 of the best places to visit in the U.S. and beyond this October. Related: 9 cool hotels for leaf peeping, from Central Park to the Rocky Mountains Zürich, Switzerland In October, Zürich comes to life with fall colors, cultural events and seasonal experiences. A major highlight is the Zurich Film Festival, running from Sept. 24 to Oct. 4. The festival features more than 100 films and a packed lineup of talks, masterclasses and galas featuring filmmakers, actors and other international guests. Just outside the city, Jucker Farm hosts its annual Pumpkin Exhibition through Oct. 25. The family-friendly event features elaborate pumpkin sculptures based on this year's "Bon Voyage" theme, along with a food festival and immersive activities including fruit picking and an apple maze. Later in the month, Expovina Weinschiffe, taking place from Oct. 29 to Nov. 12, transforms the boats at Bürkliplatz into a floating wine fair. The event brings together wine producers and visitors for tastings aboard a fleet of ships overlooking Lake Zürich. Feeling more active? Head to Üetliberg, the mountain overlooking Zürich and just a short train ride from the city center. Its network of trails is especially appealing in autumn, when colorful foliage frames sweeping views of the city, Lake Zürich, and, on clear days, the Alps. TPG tip: Situated in the city's historic Old Town and spanning nine medieval townhouses, the upscale Widder Hotel features 49 unique rooms and suites with thoughtfully preserved details, including ancient frescoes and terracotta flooring. It is also home to the two-Michelin-starred Restaurant Widder, overseen by chef Stefan Heilemann. Nightly rates in October start at $910. Book a stay of two or more nights through American Express Fine Hotels + Resorts to receive daily breakfast for two guests, guaranteed late checkout and a $100 property credit to use on qualifying food and beverages. Asheville, North Carolina While we never need a reason to plan a vacation to Asheville, a visit is also a meaningful way to support the city as it continues to recover after Hurricane Helene. With cool events and festivals happening every day, October is one of the best times of the year to visit. LaZoom's Ghosted! Adult-only Haunted Comedy Tour (Oct. 1 to 31) is a humorous and educational tour aboard the company's signature purple buses. To see Biltmore in a whole new light, check out Luminere at Biltmore (Oct. 1 to 18), an outdoor evening experience that illuminates America's Largest Home and its famous gardens with dynamic visuals and sounds. Other October picks include the family-friendly, corn-themed Eliada Corn Maze and Festival (Oct. 1 to 31); the 369 Monologue and Short Play Festival (Oct. 1 to 18), a celebration of artists of color; and the Craft Fair of the Southern Highlands (Oct. 15 to 18), one of the country's top craft events. Some of the most picturesque spots to take in Asheville's majestic fall foliage include the Blue Ridge Parkway — the views are especially stunning at Black Balsam Knob and Craggy Gardens — as well as Looking Glass Falls and Biltmore Estate. Asheville's dining and drinking scene is unpretentious, but never short on quality. Botiwalla, by James Beard Award-winning chef Meherwan Irani, celebrates India's vibrant street food culture, while Mother turns out hearty sandwiches and sweets, including a cookie bar made with its long-fermented sourdough. For a proper nightcap and dessert, head to Potential New Boyfriend, a colorful, retro-styled lounge serving natural wines and indulgent, ever-rotating ice cream flavors. TPG Tip: Following a sweeping Hurricane Helene restoration, the stately Grand Bohemian Lodge Asheville reopened last year, with updates to its locally curated art program and steakhouse, Red Stag Grill. Rooms are available from $215 or 85,000 Marriott Bonvoy points per night in October. The playful and conveniently located Moxy Asheville Downtown is also a great pick; nightly October rates start at $132 or 47,000 Marriott Bonvoy points. If glamping is your style, book the recently opened AutoCamp Asheville, with charming cabins and airstreams set on 16 scenic acres along the French Broad River. In October, accommodations are available from $256 or 70,000 Hilton Honors points per night. Related: The ultimate Blue Ridge Parkway road trip guide Saga, Japan If you want to visit Japan this fall while avoiding the biggest tourist crowds, consider Saga. This prefecture in northwestern Kyushu is gaining attention for its porcelain, sake and onsen culture — and October brings several can't-miss events. From Oct. 30 to Nov. 3, the Saga International Balloon Fiesta, Asia's largest sky sports event, fills the sky with colorful balloons, including some modeled after animals and cartoon characters. Cycling fans can also plan their trip around the 2026 Tour de Kyushu, an international road race that traverses six prefectures in Kyushu, including Saga on Oct. 10. Mild autumn weather is another draw, with daytime temperatures averaging in the mid-70s. And while Japan is already beloved for its world-class fall foliage, the season also brings a lesser-known but equally spectacular sight: peak cosmos blooms in red, white and pink. One of the best places to see them is Saga's Kinryu Park. TPG Tip: With just 84 rooms, Fairfield by Marriott Saga Ureshino Onsen offers an intimate, comfortable home base for exploring the region's legendary hot springs and rich culinary culture, including green tea and tofu. Rooms start at $78 per night or 17,000 Marriott Bonvoy points in October. Burlington, Vermont With its abundance of native trees (including sugar maples) and mountainous terrain, New England has long been one of the world's most cherished destinations for fall foliage. The catch, naturally, is the crush of crowds. This is where Burlington comes in. Set on the shores of Lake Champlain, Vermont's biggest city balances a small-town feel with urban conveniences — and, of course, spectacular scenery. Plus, the weather this time of year is blissful, averaging in the 50s. For optimal leaf-peeping, visit Centennial Woods, a 65-acre forest on the edge of the University of Vermont campus. For panoramic views of Lake Champlain, take a leisurely hike at Rock Point. Cycling enthusiasts can rent a bike from Local Motion and ride the Island Line Trail, which extends into Lake Champlain and offers spectacular views of the Adirondack Mountains. Burlington's culinary scene is tiny but mighty. The warm and deeply knowledgeable Kate Wise, a 2026 James Beard semifinalist, leads the lively bar at Hotel Vermont's Juniper Bar & Restaurant. Paul Trombly, a 2026 James Beard finalist for Best Chef: Northeast, sends out lovely, mostly plant-based dishes — order the crispy rice and lentil pancakes — at the cozy Fancy's. Fellow 2026 James Beard nominee for Outstanding Restaurateur Leslie Wells recently opened her fourth concept, Alimentari Café & Provisions. To make flying in and out even more comfortable, Leahy Burlington International Airport recently unveiled a $68 million, fossil-fuel-free expansion, complete with a brand-new terminal, more gates and additional amenities — all designed with sustainability in mind. TPG tip: With a prime address in downtown Burlington along Lake Champlain, The Harborvale debuted a few months ago with 161 guest rooms and suites in earthy tones, plus a namesake restaurant specializing in rustic, locally sourced fare. In October, nightly rates start at $274 or 55,000 Marriott Bonvoy points. Vienna If you're an art and culture lover, October is one of the best months to visit Austria's capital. But if you only have a weekend to spare, make it Oct. 3 to 4. This way, you can combine the final days of Vienna Design Week (Sept. 25 to Oct. 4) — one of Europe's top design festivals, celebrating its 20th anniversary this year — with the Long Night of Museums (Oct. 3), when a single ticket gives you access to museums and cultural institutions staying open late for one evening. It's also the opening weekend of the Vienna Drag Festival (Oct. 3 to18). Viennale (Oct. 22 to Nov. 3), Austria's premier international film festival, and Design District (Oct. 9 to 11), an annual showcase of interior design and furniture, are also worth checking out. As October is harvest season in the city's vineyards, set aside some time for wine-related experiences: sipping Wiener Gemischter Satz, Vienna's signature wine, at Heurigen (traditional wine taverns); hiking through the vineyards of Kahlenberg and Nussberg; and hopping aboard the Heurigen Express, a miniature train that loops through the city's wine-growing districts. In case you didn't know, Vienna is an under-the-radar destination for fall foliage. With approximately 1,000 parks and gardens, there are plenty of spots — local picks include the historic Schönbrunn Palace Gardens and the city parks of Stadtpark, Volksgarten and Burggarten — to immerse yourself in the seasonal scenery. TPG Tip: Housed in a beautifully restored 20th-century Art Nouveau building, Mandarin Oriental Vienna blends a posh, residential-style design with all the hallmarks the Hong Kong–based hospitality brand is known for: personalized service, a holistic approach to wellness — including Vienna's largest indoor pool — and elegant dining concepts that attract guests and locals alike. October rates for this American Express Fine Hotels + Resorts member start at $794 per night. Aruba Aruba lives up to its nickname, "One Happy Island," thanks to its consistently sunny weather, location outside the hurricane belt, cooling trade winds and silky beaches. No wonder it's such a popular year-round destination. If your travel dates are flexible, consider arriving during Aruba's low season in October. You'll enjoy lower hotel rates and fewer crowds while experiencing one of the island's biggest events: the Autentico Aruba Culinary Festival. Taking place Oct. 3 to 11, the festival celebrates the culinary traditions of the island's diverse population, reflecting its more than 100 nationalities. Highlights include special prix-fixe menus during Restaurant Week, chef-hosted Bucket List Experiences and the grand finale, The Pavilion. Other October events to mark on your calendar include the inaugural Leyenda del Dorado Aruba (Oct. 9 to 11), a three-day international mountain bike race across the island's craggy terrain, and Interpaso (Oct. 31 to Nov. 1), an international Paso Fino horse competition. Don't forget to pick up some of Aruba Aloe's world-famous skincare — perfect for soothing your sun-kissed skin and equally great for gift-giving — before you head home. TPG Tip: Based on the hotel-within-a-hotel concept, the new The Westerly at Hilton Aruba Caribbean Resort is an oceanfront tower with 161 crisp, airy rooms — the beds are especially dreamy — plus Terrace on 10, an adults-only rooftop retreat available for an additional fee. The indoor-outdoor space pairs stunning waterfront views with well-crafted drinks and all-day dining. Naturally, guests of The Westerly also have access to everything the Hilton resort has to offer, including the eforea Spa, casino and prime stretch of Palm Beach. Rooms are available from $743 or 243,000 Hilton Honors points per night in October. Lancaster County, Pennsylvania If you're after a scenic, culturally rich and delicious fall getaway — just a three-hour Amtrak ride from New York City — consider Lancaster County in south-central Pennsylvania. Home to the oldest and largest Amish community in the United States, the area is known for its bucolic landscape of rolling farmland, quiet streams and historic covered bridges. You'll likely find yourself sharing the road with Amish horse-drawn buggies, too. To learn more about Amish culture, visit the Amish Village, where an authentic 1840 farmhouse, one-room schoolhouse and other historic structures offer a glimpse into traditional Amish life. Opened in May in downtown Lancaster, the Thaddeus Stevens & Lydia Hamilton Smith Center is a museum and educational center highlighting the lives and legacies of abolitionist and civil rights advocate Thaddeus Stevens and his partner, Lydia Hamilton Smith. Since 1954, Kitchen Kettle Village has grown into a charming destination in its own right, with more than 40 shops, including the iconic Jam & Relish Kitchen, Kling House Restaurant and residential-style accommodations. Lancaster County's restaurant scene offers an enticing mix of old and new. For casual bites, check out Lancaster Central Market, the oldest continuously operated public market in America, and Southern Market, just a few blocks away. Nathan Flaim, a 2026 James Beard Award finalist for Best Chef: Mid-Atlantic, has grown Luca into a popular destination for exceptional housemade pastas and small plates that showcase Lancaster's rich bounty. Passerine and Vécu are equally charming brunch options, while Front Porch Baking Co. specializes in loaves and pastries baked with Pennsylvania-grown grains. No trip to Lancaster, however, would be complete without visiting a smorgasbord, a massive buffet including Pennsylvania Dutch comfort foods like potato filling, chicken corn soup and shoofly pie. TPG Tip: Taking up residence in the former Wilbur Chocolate Factory, the 74-key Wilbur Lititz, Tapestry Collection by Hilton retains many of the historic structure's original details — timber beams, exposed brick and arched windows — while incorporating modern touches, from the chocolate scent that infuses the lobby to Kōle Chophouse, a relaxed steakhouse serving Japanese Wagyu fired on a Josper charcoal grill. Nightly October rates start at $216 or 63,000 Hilton Honors points. Seychelles Though Seychelles makes for a great warm-weather vacation any time of year, October holds even more appeal for those seeking sublime weather — hot, sunny and relatively dry, with little wind or rain. The month is also ideal for catching big fish, such as barracuda and various tuna species. The island nation is also renowned for its diverse birdlife, and October provides an opportune time to spot migratory shorebirds like Pacific golden plovers and breeding seabirds, including sooty terns. The Creole Festival, an annual celebration of the archipelago's unique tapestry of African, European and Asian influences, will be hosted in the country's lively capital of Victoria during the last week of October. TPG tip: The all-villa Cheval Blanc Seychelles marks the sixth property in LVMH's swanky Cheval Blanc portfolio, and the first in Africa. Receive daily breakfast for two, late checkout and more when you book via the Amex Fine Hotels + Resorts program. Nightly rates in October start at $2,600. Puebla, Mexico Puebla is the antidote for those weary of touristy Mexico City and Tulum. Despite being Mexico's fourth-biggest city, Puebla balances everything you want from a well-rounded vacation destination — restaurants, shopping, history — with a neighborly, small-town feel. October is one of the best times to visit, as the month marks the transition from the rainy season to the dry season, with average daytime highs in the mid- to high 70s. Even better? It's easy to experience the best of Puebla in one weekend. Meander through the city's UNESCO-listed historic center, filled with colorful 16th- and 17th-century churches and other religious structures. As Puebla is the birthplace of mole poblano, the famously complex sweet-savory sauce, try as many versions as possible while you're in town. Some of the best can be found at the Michelin Guide-recommended Augurio, from beloved local chef Ángel Vázquez, as well as Comal and Mural de los Poblanos. It's also worth shopping for talavera, the region's colorful, hand-painted ceramics. TPG tip: A member of American Express Fine Hotels + Resorts, Banyan Tree Puebla is a 78-room property that celebrates Pueblan culture from its design to its offerings, including the highly recommended mole cooking class. Rooms in October start at $195 per night. Brisbane, Australia No longer hiding in the shadows of Sydney and Melbourne, Brisbane — Australia's third-largest city and Queensland's capital — has blossomed into a worldly yet laid-back destination. With pleasant October temperatures hovering in the mid- to high 70s, Brisbane is an urban paradise for outdoor lovers, whether you want to soak in the rays at Streets Beach (a unique human-made beach) or get up close to wildlife at Lone Pine Koala Sanctuary. The city's restaurant landscape has also been attracting attention, with the ambitious tasting-menu concept Exhibition, wood-fired Agnes and intimate August, housed in a refurbished 137-year-old heritage church, leading the charge. TPG tip: Since 2018, the W Brisbane has been one of the city's hippest places to hang your hat. Rooms are available from $360 or 48,000 Marriott Bonvoy points per night in October.

item.title: Carnival launches new card with 50,000-point bonus and ability to earn cruise status
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 2.85
Carnival launches new card with 50,000-point bonus and ability to earn cruise status There's nothing like sailing away and enjoying a day at sea under the sun, watching the waves go by and heading toward a waiting port filled with fun and excursions. And if you happened to have paid for some or all of the sailing with points, it's that much sweeter. Carnival actually just made it easier to get that much closer to your next sailing with the launch of the all-new Carnival Rewards™ Mastercard®. The card is launching with a limited-time offer of 50,000 bonus Carnival Rewards Points after spending $1,000 in the first 90 days* and lets you earn points on your everyday spending directly into the Carnival Rewards program. That means it is easier than ever to redeem points for things like your next onboard cocktail, excursion, spa treatment or even an entire cruise. Additionally, for the first time ever, spending on a Carnival Rewards Mastercard will also earn you Status Qualifying Stars toward status in the Carnival Rewards program. That's a first, not just for Carnival, but across the cruise industry. Plus, you'll also get special financing for six months on Carnival bookings that you put on your Carnival Rewards Mastercard. Here's how it all works. Basics of the new Carnival Rewards program There are now two currencies to understand in the new Carnival Rewards program: points and stars. Points are the redeemable currency. Think of them like airline frequent flyer miles. You can earn them on eligible Carnival spending and with the Carnival Rewards Mastercard, then redeem them toward everything from spa treatments and excursions to the cruise itself. Stars work differently. Rather than redeeming them, stars are how you qualify for Carnival's status tiers and their associated perks. Carnival Rewards members earn 3 stars per dollar on eligible Carnival purchases, while cardmembers can earn an additional 1 star per dollar spent on the Carnival Rewards Mastercard, both on cruises and everyday purchases. How to earn and use Carnival Rewards points You can now earn Carnival Rewards points both on Carnival cruises and when using the Carnival Rewards Mastercard. - All Carnival Rewards members earn 3 points per dollar on Carnival cruises - Carnival Rewards Mastercard cardmembers earn an additional 3 points per dollar on eligible Carnival cruises, for a total of 6 points per dollar - Carnival Rewards Mastercard cardmembers also earn 2 points per dollar at eligible restaurants and grocery stores and 1 point per dollar on all other purchases And with the card's welcome offer, you can also earn 50,000 bonus points after spending $1,000 on your card in the first 90 days, giving you a great jump start to lots of redemption options. So what can you get with all those Carnival Rewards points? That's where the fun part comes in. Want an onboard frozen pina colada? That's 1,357 Carnival Rewards points. Or how about an onboard Teppanyaki dinner? It'll only cost you 2,400 points per person. (Redemption values are as of the writing of this review but subject to change.) Are you thinking something more adventurous, like a stingray beach encounter? That's also just 2,400 points. Or go bigger: A three-night Bahamas cruise starts at 13,499 points for two, plus taxes and fees. In other words, the limited-time bonus of 50,000 points can actually go a pretty long way. Based on the sample redemptions given, Carnival Rewards points delivered roughly 1 to 2 cents per point in value, though the exact value will vary depending on how you redeem them.** **Point values accurate at the time of writing. What makes the Carnival Rewards Mastercard stand out It's not just the points you can redeem that make the Carnival Rewards Mastercard interesting; it's also that it earns Status Qualifying Stars. It's the first cruise credit card to offer cardmembers the option to earn points and status just by using the card for everyday spending. You'll earn one Status Qualifying Star and at least one redeemable point per dollar spent. That means every time you use your card, you're one step closer to your next points redemption and even unlocking perks like complimentary beverages and early check-in times with your next status tier. On top of that, you can get 2,500 bonus points every anniversary year you have the Carnival Rewards Mastercard after spending $2,000 on purchases. Earning Carnival status while not cruising The revamped Carnival Rewards program makes earning and using points very easy. You can use as few as 1 point toward booking a cruise, redeem your points for onboard meals or drinks, or even cover an excursion. But it is also pretty exciting to see Carnival follow a model that many at TPG already know and love from airline loyalty programs, where loyalty isn't something that you only earn when you are on a trip. You can now make progress toward Carnival's Gold, Platinum and Diamond status levels while you're using the card at the grocery store, dining out or stocking up on your favorite cruise essentials. Gold status requires 10,000 Stars. Since the Carnival Rewards Mastercard earns 1 Star per dollar spent, you can make progress toward that threshold even when you're not on a ship. If you earned all 10,000 Stars through card spending during the initial roughly two-year qualification period, that would work out to an average of about $5,000 in card spending per year. Then the perks really start to ramp up at the Platinum level with goodies such as preferred dining time, two complimentary beverages and priority embarkation and debarkation, which are actually pretty great perks that help you get to the fun that much faster. | Status | Stars required | Example perks | |---|---|---| | Red | Entry level | Complimentary bottle of water | | Gold | 10,000 Stars | Complimentary 1.5L bottle of water; complimentary beverage on cruises of 5+ days | | Platinum | 50,000 Stars | Preferred dining time; two complimentary beverages; complimentary wash and fold; priority embarkation and debarkation | | Diamond | 100,000 Stars | Guaranteed Main Dining time; dedicated Diamond member support; special event invitation from the Captain | You have two years to earn status (from the program's launch in Sept. 2026 until Dec. 31, 2028) and then two years to enjoy the perks while you are making progress toward the next two years' worth of status. Those who had Fun Points in the previous Carnival Mastercard program will have those converted into Carnival Rewards points. Bottom line Your next Carnival cruise may only last seven days, but you can now still easily spend your days back at home on land, racking up Carnival Rewards points and Stars. The new program really takes rewards earning beyond just the time you are at sea and was built with the Carnival Rewards Mastercard in mind. This means the card can now play a pretty major role in not only how you earn points to use on your next Carnival cruise, but also the Stars that can help you unlock that next status level in the program, too. This is a pretty big step for a cruise loyalty program and one that will help some Carnival cruisers unlock more rewards and perks on their future cruises. The Carnival Rewards Mastercard is issued by Barclays Bank Delaware pursuant to a license from Mastercard International Incorporated. Mastercard, World Mastercard, World Elite Mastercard, and the circles design are registered trademarks of Mastercard International Incorporated. Learn more about the Carnival Rewards Mastercard. Terms apply. *Offer ends Dec. 30, 2026.

item.title: What's it like staying at Hyatt's new Caption branded hotels in Osaka and Tokyo
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 2.72
What's it like staying at Hyatt's new Caption branded hotels in Osaka and Tokyo One of World of Hyatt's newest brands is called Caption, and after a stay at two of only six properties worldwide, I can safely say it captured my heart. Hyatt describes the brand as "of the community," and that's definitely what they are going for at the two Caption hotels in Japan that I visited. I booked two nights in Tokyo and two nights in Osaka so that TPG could get a sense of the new brand and share with readers why they might want to choose these hotels in the heart of two of the country's largest cities. Related: The 11 best hotels in Tokyo for your next Japan getaway The best part of the stay? The price tag. Japan hotels can be notoriously expensive, but the Caption by Hyatt Namba Osaka and Kabutocho Tokyo were quite reasonable. I'd definitely recommend these hotels, especially if you are going to be mostly sightseeing during your stay. Here's a look at each property, how much it costs and why you might want to consider it on your next Japan adventure. Caption by Hyatt Kabutocho Tokyo I spent two nights at the Caption by Hyatt Kabutocho in Tokyo. The hotel opened late in 2025, so it's still looking brand-new and in tip-top shape. The building itself is made of a combination of wood and steel as part of a low-carbon structure, and there's an obvious and genuine effort toward sustainability. The hotel was even awarded Tokyo's first-ever DBJ Green Building Certification. Caption by Hyatt Kabutocho sits in an interesting location, within the city's business district. It's actually close to the Tokyo Stock Exchange, but it's not far from the famous shopping districts of Ginza and Nihombashi as well. There are several nearby subway lines, and Tokyo Station is about a five-minute taxi ride away. The hotel has 195 rooms, including one suite. I didn't bother asking for the suite, despite my Hyatt Globalist status, though the friendly receptionist who checked me in told me I'd been upgraded to a deluxe high-floor room. Non-suite rooms range from 269 to 301 square feet. Overall, the room was great — a bit on the small side, but no smaller than several other Tokyo Hyatt hotels that I've stayed in over the years. The bed was comfortable with a variety of fluffy and firm pillows. There were outlets throughout the room, including next to the bed on both sides. Views were fun, with sweeping city vistas and even a peek at Tokyo Tower off in the distance. A blackout curtain kept the light out with the pull of a beaded string. There was also a separate seating area with a small loveseat, a chair and a small desktop. A bulletin board had magnets and a notepad and a pen, and there were cute little signs throughout the room. There was also a pegboard with several shoe care accessories. I don't love the open-air concept closets, but it was fairly practical with a small ironing board and steamer, four drawers (one of which held a safe) and darling pajama sets. There was also a first for me: A humidifier in the room. There was a small fridge in a cabinet that also held a kettle and some glasses. On top of the cabinet was a pitcher (you can fill up on filtered water on every floor) and a small ice bucket. The bathroom was on the smaller side, but fine. There was a single sink and a walk-in shower. Apotheke amenities were available in large bottles. The water pressure was excellent, though there was only a wand showerhead. There was also a full Toto bidet toilet. There was also anything else you might need for free available at the check-in counter, including toothpaste, shave cream, moisturizer and even a packaged bath towel. On the second floor, there was a large living space where the hotel intended for folks to gather in a community style. I didn't see anyone in there any of the times I visited (that's where you'll find the ice machine). There was a small balcony there with city street views, but no outdoor seating. On the same floor, there was a decent-sized gym with plenty of brand-new Lifefitness equipment, including elliptical machines and treadmills, along with a small selection of free weights. The lobby was where most of the action was happening at the hotel. That's where meals were served all throughout the day, and it was always busy. It's a Caption signature space called "Talk Shop." The lobby looks at it like a communal space where everyone can escape their small rooms and hang out. There were multiple seating areas and lots of friendly staff manning the various counters and the check-in desks. I can see this being very popular, not only with the younger demographic Caption is targeting, but also with people who live in the nearby community. The hotel calls it a "lively, flexible space where a restaurant, coffee shop, bar and co-working space all come together." I got free breakfast both days of my stay as a World of Hyatt Globalist, but there is a set breakfast menu that will cost you between $17 and $20 depnding on your order. I tried a traditional Japanese breakfast one day and overnight oats on another. Both meals were delicious. The one thing that was a glaring omission in my book? There were no espresso drinks available. Drip coffee was all that was available during my stay. The most interesting tidbit of my stay was being awoken at 2 a.m. with an alert of an incoming earthquake on my phone. Moments later, the room was shaking quite hard. It was a 5.9 tremor. Enough to shake the room, but no damage, and the hotel didn't even make an announcement. Normal stuff in Japan, I guess. View this post on Instagram I stayed two nights at this Category 5 Hyatt property, where points bookings generally run 20,000 or 25,000 World of Hyatt points per night. Cash rates are much more reasonable here. I saw prices as low as $187 per night, though TPG paid $542 for two nights in the high summer season. Caption by Hyatt Namba Osaka I have similar positive things to say about my stay at Caption by Hyatt Nammba Osaka, but two additional things made it even better. First, the location. The 167-room Caption in Osaka is in the heart of the bustling Namba neighborhood with easy access to the incredible variety of street food and shopping that this wonderful neighborhood enjoys. Related: Hyatt's 1st Caption hotel is open: My time walking (and sleeping) in Memphis It was only a 15-minute walk to the world-famous Dotonbori Street with its flashing neon signs and shops selling everything from sushi to streetwear. This is also where you'll find the famous "running man" neon billboard. This is like the Times Square of Osaka. I loved it. The second standout feature was the laundry machines on the second floor. At this point in my two-week Asia trip, I was in desperate need of fresh laundry. The machines are coin-operated and a bit pricey, but it was so nice to have clean clothes. I spent about $8 on a load of laundry (detergent is included, and the machine fills automatically). Despite being in a noisy neighborhood, the new construction of the Caption meant there was no noise at night, allowing for a great night's sleep. Though my queen-sized bed was a bit firm, I still slept well. The 10th-floor room was on the small side, but it did have a separate seating area with two chairs. City views were charming, and blackout curtains worked well here, too. Like the Caption in Tokyo, outlets were plentiful, and there was fun pop art throughout the room. Check out the samurai sword clothing rack in the open-air closet. The bathroom was tiny but had a Toto bidet toilet and a shower with both a wand and a rainhead, with excellent water pressure. Just like at the Tokyo hotel, there was a gym, but that was really it for major amenities. It was on the smaller side, but I did manage to use some of the free weights. The main floor held the lobby and the signature Talk Shop. The space was huge, even when filled with stored luggage. I enjoyed a Western-style breakfast. There were plenty of seating areas, including a large outdoor space (though it was too hot to try while I was there). Interestingly, both hotels had self-check-in machines, but the front desks were always fully staffed with friendly employees, and I didn't see anyone actually using them to check in. I paid just $234.95 for two nights at this Category 3 property. I'd call that a great deal, but you can also book it for as few as 8,000 World of Hyatt points per night. Cash rates are as low as $99 a night, but more often around $129. It's the only Hyatt option in Osaka for World of Hyatt fans. Both hotels were fully wheelchair accessible, with some ADA-compliant rooms. Elevators were accessible with grab bars, Braille signage and lowered buttons. Bottom line I'd happily stay at both the Hyatt Kabutocho Tokyo and the Caption by Hyatt Namba Osaka again anytime. The relaxed vibes and quiet, comfortable rooms are all you need for a stay in the big cities when what you'll mostly be doing is sightseeing anyway. Central locations make visiting the city easy, with subways and even some major attractions a short walk away. While the lack of a long list of amenities will put some people off, the budget-friendly bill at the end of the stay makes these properties shine. Related reading: - Ocean oasis: A review of the Andaz Maui at Wailea Resort in Hawaii - World of Hyatt gold: What it's really like to stay at the Andaz Munich Schwabinger Tor - I didn't expect to love World of Hyatt, but here's why I do - What it's like staying at the Park Hyatt New York — a gorgeous flagship property bookable on points

item.title: Capital One Venture Rewards current offer: 75,000 miles plus a $300 credit for Capital One Travel
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 2.60
Capital One Venture Rewards current offer: 75,000 miles plus a $300 credit for Capital One Travel Editor's Note The Capital One Venture Rewards Credit Card is a great choice for beginners and experienced points-and-miles enthusiasts who want an easy way to earn miles with minimal effort — all for an affordable $95 annual fee. The Venture Rewards card's current welcome offer is especially compelling: Earn 75,000 bonus miles after spending $4,000 on purchases within the first three months from account opening. Plus, you'll receive a $300 credit upon approval to use on hotel and vacation rentals booked through Capital One Travel in the first cardholder year. Here's what the offer is worth and what to know before applying. Capital One Venture Rewards welcome offer New Capital One Venture Rewards cardholders can earn 75,000 bonus miles after spending $4,000 on purchases within the first three months from account opening. Plus, you'll receive a $300 credit upon approval to use on hotel and vacation rentals booked through Capital One Travel in the first cardholder year. Including the credit, this offer is worth $1,688, per TPG's September 2026 valuations. In terms of miles alone, this is the standard welcome bonus on the card. However, the inclusion of the $300 credit makes this offer among the most valuable we've seen. For comparison, previous welcome offers have gone as high as 100,000 miles after meeting the minimum spending requirements (no longer available), but with no credit. It's possible to squeeze even more from that bonus if you redeem Capital One miles for maximum value, thanks to their impressive roster of 15-plus transfer partners. Who is eligible for the Venture Rewards welcome bonus? There are some eligibility requirements to keep in mind before applying. You don't want to waste a hard pull on your credit report if you aren't eligible for the current offer. First, if you've previously earned a welcome bonus on the Venture Rewards, you won't be able to earn another one for 48 months. Note that this is 48 months from the date you received your bonus, not from the date you were approved. In addition, if you previously earned a welcome bonus on the Capital One Venture X Rewards Credit Card, you will more than likely not be eligible to earn a welcome bonus on the Venture Rewards. Capital One may consider multiple factors when deciding whether to approve you; for a deeper dive into its application requirements, check out our full guide. Related: The best Capital One credit cards Earning Capital One miles This card earns at least 2 miles per dollar spent on all purchases. So, by spending $4,000 on it to earn the welcome bonus, you'd earn at least 83,000 miles in the first few months, including the welcome bonus. And since the Venture Rewards earns 5 miles per dollar spent on car rentals, hotels and vacation rentals booked through Capital One Travel, it's possible to earn even more miles while working toward your welcome bonus. While some travel credit cards may earn slightly higher rates on select categories such as groceries or dining, the draw here is the simplicity and guarantee of earning at least 2 miles per dollar spent on anything you buy without the need to memorize multiple bonus spending categories. Related: Why I keep the Capital One Venture Rewards card in my wallet What can Capital One Miles get you? Your total value from this welcome bonus depends largely on how you redeem your miles. There are two key options: - Redeem for 1 cent apiece toward travel - Redeem by transferring to Capital One's 15-plus partner airlines and hotels (our recommendation) When converting your miles to hotel points or airline miles, most partners offer a 1:1 transfer ratio, though a couple of partners have different ratios. You can get great sweet spot redemptions by transferring miles to programs like Air Canada Aeroplan and Air France-KLM Flying Blue. For example, TPG's editor-in-chief, Nick Ewen, transferred 117,000 Capital One miles to Emirates Skywards to upgrade himself and two family members to Emirates first class. This broke down to 39,000 miles per person, a reasonable cost for the upgrade. If you don't want to transfer your miles, you can redeem them by booking a trip through Capital One Travel. These redemptions can be very handy in a world where you may be renting recreational vehicles, booking vacation home rentals or securing a cabin close to home more often than hopping on a flight to the other side of the world. Related: Cashing in Capital One miles? How to get the maximum value when redeeming miles Other Venture Rewards perks The Capital One Venture Rewards doesn't offer the same benefits as more premium travel rewards cards, including its upscale sibling, the Capital One Venture X Rewards. But for its modest $95 annual fee, the Venture Rewards provides some useful benefits: - An up to $120 statement credit for Global Entry or TSA PreCheck application fees - Car rental insurance - Complimentary concierge service - Extended warranty protection - No foreign transaction fees Related: Chase Sapphire Preferred Card vs. Capital One Venture Rewards Bottom line The Capital One Venture Rewards remains a strong option for travelers who value simplicity. It earns at least 2 miles per dollar spent on purchases and gives cardholders access to Capital One's airline and hotel transfer partners, all for a $95 annual fee. Plus, the current welcome offer includes a solid haul of miles and a $300 credit for Capital One Travel, one of the best offers we've seen. Just remember to use your credit in the first cardholder year, or you'll forfeit the value. To learn more, read our full review of the Capital One Venture Rewards card. Learn more: Capital One Venture Rewards Credit Card For Capital One products listed on this page, some of the benefits may be provided by Visa® or Mastercard® and may vary by product. See the respective Guide to Benefits for details, as terms and exclusions apply.

item.title: Ink Business Unlimited vs. Spark Cash Select: Which simple business cash-back card wins?
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 2.50
Ink Business Unlimited vs. Spark Cash Select: Which simple business cash-back card wins? As a business owner myself, I've spent more brain power than I'd like to admit thinking about which credit cards can help me get more out of my business spending. Two cards that often come up when you're looking for a simple, no-annual-fee business card are the Ink Business Unlimited® Credit Card (see rates and fees) and Capital One Spark Cash Select — and it's easy to see why they're competitors. Both keep earning simple, offer tools and benefits for business owners and don't charge an annual fee. At the end of the day, though, the Ink Business Unlimited has an edge for most business owners, especially if you can pair it with an eligible Chase Ultimate Rewards card. I've already put more thought into business credit cards than any reasonable person should, so let me break it down for you. Ink Business Unlimited vs. Spark Cash Select: At a glance | | Ink Business Unlimited | Capital One Spark Cash Select | |---|---|---| | Annual fee | $0 | $0 | | Welcome bonus | Earn $1,000 cash back after spending $8,000 on purchases in the first four months after account opening. | Earn a one-time $750 cash bonus after spending $6,000 on purchases within the first three months from account opening. | | Employee card fee | $0 | $0 | | Base earning rate | Unlimited 1.5% cash back | Unlimited 1.5% cash back | Quick picks by business type | Best for ... | Card | |---|---| | Business owners who already earn Chase Ultimate Rewards points | Ink Business Unlimited | | Those who want more time to finance a large purchase | Ink Business Unlimited | | Those who already earn Capital One miles | Capital One Spark Cash Select | | Those who make purchases abroad | Capital One Spark Cash Select | Ink Business Unlimited vs. Spark Cash Select: Welcome bonus The Ink Business Unlimited currently offers $1,000 cash back after spending $8,000 on purchases in the first four months after account opening. The Spark Cash Select offers a one-time $750 cash bonus after spending $6,000 on purchases within the first three months from account opening. The Ink's bonus is $250 higher, but you'll need to spend an additional $2,000 to earn it. If that level of spending is already normal for your business, the extra $250 is an easy win. But don't spend more than you otherwise would just to chase a bigger bonus. Eligibility is important to consider, too. Chase's application terms say the Ink Business Unlimited bonus may not be available if you've ever had this card or another no-annual-fee Chase business card. Meanwhile, Capital One states that the bonus may not be available to existing or previous Capital One Business cardholders. Winner: Ink Business Unlimited. Assuming you can comfortably meet the higher spending requirement, the extra $250 makes it the better offer. Related: The ultimate guide to credit card application restrictions Ink Business Unlimited vs. Spark Cash Select: Benefits Neither card is going to wow you with a long list of amazing perks — but that's hardly a surprise for a business card with no annual fee. However, both options offer more protection than you might expect, including extended warranty coverage and rental car insurance. | Benefit | Ink Business Unlimited | Capital One Spark Cash Select | |---|---|---| | Employee cards | No additional cost | No additional cost | | Auto rental coverage | Primary for business rentals; up to $60,000 for most eligible vehicles | Primary for eligible business and international rentals* | | Purchase protection | Up to $10,000 per item for 120 days; $50,000 annual account limit | Up to $10,000 per item for 90 days; $50,000 annual account limit* | | Extended warranty protection | Adds one year to eligible warranties of three years or less | Doubles eligible warranties of 12 months or less, up to one additional year* | | Roadside assistance | Yes; cardholder pays for services | Yes; cardholder pays for services | | Foreign transaction fee | 3% | None | *Capital One Mastercard benefits are subject to issuer participation. Check your card's Guide to Benefits for applicable coverage. There's quite a bit of overlap between the two cards. Both offer extended warranty protection, purchase protection and rental car coverage, although the exact terms and coverage limits differ. The Ink Business Unlimited has an edge on purchase protection. Eligible purchases are covered against damage or theft for 120 days (up to $10,000 per item and $50,000 per account per year), whereas the Spark Cash Select only covers up to 90 days (with the same limits). The rental car comparison is closer than it first appears. Ink provides primary coverage when renting for business purposes, with reimbursement of up to $60,000 for theft and collision damage for most eligible vehicles. Depending on your card's applicable Mastercard benefits, Spark's MasterRental coverage can also be primary for eligible business rentals and rentals outside your home country. With primary coverage, you shouldn't have to file a claim with your personal auto insurer first. Spark, meanwhile, has an advantage if your business takes you abroad. It charges no foreign transaction fees, compared with 3% on the Ink Business Unlimited. Winner: Tie. Ink offers longer purchase protection and straightforward primary rental car coverage for eligible business rentals, while Spark counters with competitive protections and no foreign transaction fees. Related: Why nearly every purchase should be on a credit card How to earn and redeem rewards with the Ink Business Unlimited vs. Spark Cash Select At first glance, there's not much separating these cards when it comes to earning rewards. Both earn at least 1.5% back on everyday purchases, with no spending caps to track. | Purchase | Ink Business Unlimited | Capital One Spark Cash Select | |---|---|---| | Everyday purchases | 1.5% cash back | 1.5% cash back | | Lyft rides | 5% cash back through (Sept. 30, 2027) | 1.5% cash back | | Hotels and rental cars booked through Capital One Business Travel | 1.5% cash back | 5% cash back | The Spark Cash Select has the edge on hotels and rental cars booked through Capital One Business Travel, earning 5% cash back. The Ink Business Unlimited has a 5% category for Lyft rides through (Sept. 30, 2027), but it's a temporary perk with a much narrower use case. Winner on earning: Spark Cash Select. Both cards earn the same 1.5% on everyday purchases, but Spark's 5% return on Capital One Business Travel bookings gives it a leg up. Redeeming rewards Cash back is the easiest way to use rewards with either card. But if you're willing to do a little more work, both cards have the potential to become much more useful for travel. You can convert the cash back you earn on the Ink Business Unlimited to points with an eligible Ultimate Rewards card, such as the Ink Business Preferred® Credit Card (see rates and fees) or Chase Sapphire Reserve for Business℠ (see rates and fees). Doing so lets you transfer those points to Chase's airline and hotel partners. The Spark Cash Select works similarly. If you have an eligible Capital One miles-earning card, you can convert your cash back into Capital One miles and transfer those miles to Capital One's airline and hotel partners. Neither program is automatically better for travel, either. Chase and Capital One have different airline and hotel transfer partners, so the better option depends largely on which programs you actually use. If you already earn rewards with Chase or Capital One, that's an even stronger reason to stick with the same program and combine your rewards rather than starting from scratch with the other. Winner on redeeming: Tie. Both cards make cash back easy, while pairing either with an eligible card can open the door to transferable travel rewards. Related: How (and why) you should earn transferable credit card points Can I have both the Ink Business Unlimited and Spark Cash Select? Yes. Since one card is issued by Chase and the other by Capital One, there's nothing stopping you from holding both. But you'll still need to qualify for each card individually. For the Ink Business Unlimited, keep Chase's 5/24 rule in mind. You'll need to be under 5/24 to qualify, though most business cards won't count toward your 5/24 total. Capital One doesn't have a publicly stated rule comparable to Chase's 5/24 rule, but you'll still need to meet the issuer's current application requirements to qualify for the Spark Cash Select. But do you actually need both? Probably not. Since both earn at least 1.5% cash back on all purchases, there's a lot of overlap. And with several cash-back cards earning 2% on everyday spending, neither is the strongest choice based on its base earning rate alone. These cards are a better fit if you value simplicity, want to avoid an annual fee or already earn rewards with Chase or Capital One. But if you're starting from scratch, I'd look at options like the Wells Fargo Signify Business Cash® Card (see rates and fees), which earns 2% cash rewards on purchases, or the The American Express Blue Business Cash® Card, which earns 2% cash back on all eligible purchases (up to $50,000 per calendar year, then 1% back on all purchases). Related: The best business credit cards to add to your wallet Should I get the Ink Business Unlimited or Spark Cash Select? Choose the Ink Business Unlimited if you already have or want to get a Chase Ultimate Rewards-points earning credit card. Choose the Spark Cash Select if you regularly make international purchases or book hotels and rental cars through Capital One Business Travel. It's also a natural fit if you already have a Capital One travel card and can combine your rewards for more redemption options. Related: Your guide to the Chase Ink Business credit cards Bottom line After weighing it all, Chase's Ink Business Unlimited comes out ahead, but just barely. Its useful protections and the potential to get more from your rewards by pairing it with another Ultimate Rewards card give it the edge. Still, Capital One's Spark Cash Select puts up a good fight. With no foreign transaction fees and 5% back on hotels and rental cars booked through Capital One Business Travel, it could be the better fit for some business owners. To learn more, read our full review of the Ink Business Unlimited and our full review of the Capital One Spark Cash Select. Apply here: Ink Business Unlimited Credit Card Learn more: Capital One Spark Cash Select For Capital One products listed on this page, some of the benefits may be provided by Visa® or Mastercard® and may vary by product. See the respective Guide to Benefits for details, as terms and exclusions apply.

item.title: Best-ever offer: How good is the Citi / AAdvantage Executive Mastercard 125K-mile bonus?
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 2.39
Best-ever offer: How good is the Citi / AAdvantage Executive Mastercard 125K-mile bonus? Editor's Note If you're serious about earning a ton of American Airlines AAdvantage miles and receiving elitelike benefits, the Citi® / AAdvantage® Executive World Legend Mastercard® (see rates and fees) likely deserves a spot in your wallet. The card recently received a refresh, adding new benefits while increasing its annual fee to $695. Beyond the welcome bonus, this card delivers real value through accelerated miles and Loyalty Points earning, a complimentary Admirals Club airport lounge membership, valuable statement credits, priority airport perks and inflight savings that can help offset that cost. With the card's welcome bonus now hitting the highest offer we've ever seen on this card — TPG readers are asking: How good is the Citi AAdvantage Executive limited time 125,000-mile offer, earned after spending $15,000 on purchases within the first five months from account opening? Here's my take on why this card remains so rewarding. How common is a 125,000‑mile welcome bonus on the Citi / AA Executive? Over the last seven years, the Citi / AAdvantage Executive reached the 100,000-mile mark only four times, making this new 125,000-mile offer truly exceptional. The previous high of 100,000 bonus miles was most recently offered in March of this year, and required spending $10,000 within the first three months from account opening (no longer available). The current offer requires more total spending — $15,000 instead of $10,000 — but gives you five months instead of three to meet the requirement. That works out to an average of $3,000 in monthly spending, compared with roughly $3,333 per month under the previous highest offer. So, while you'll need to spend an additional $5,000 overall, you have more time to do it and will earn an additional 25,000 AAdvantage miles. The last time the card hit 100,000 miles, it was available for less than three months. If you've been waiting for a reason to apply, this is it. Who is eligible for the 125,000‑mile welcome bonus on the Citi / AA Executive? To be approved for the Citi / AAdvantage Executive, a credit score of 670 or higher is recommended. Citi doesn't limit the total number of credit cards you can hold, but it does limit the overall credit line it will provide you. You can only apply for one card every eight days, and no more than two cards in 65 days. Citi's 48-month rule means you can't earn a welcome bonus on the Citi / AA Executive if you've received one on this card within the past four years. Note that the clock starts ticking from the time you receive the welcome bonus, not when you are approved for or activate the card. Related: The ultimate guide to credit card application restrictions How much are 125,000 AAdvantage miles worth? According to TPG's September 2026 valuations, AAdvantage miles are worth 1.45 cents each. That means the 125,000-mile welcome bonus on the Citi / AA Executive is worth an impressive $1,813. I'm drawn to AAdvantage miles for their flexibility and value. I like to use them for domestic American Airlines flights across the U.S., transatlantic trips to Europe, getaways to Mexico, and premium cabin redemptions on partner carriers like Finnair, Japan Airlines and Qantas. The AAdvantage program blends award chart and dynamic pricing models. When booking American Airlines or Fiji Airways flights, you'll encounter dynamic pricing where award costs fluctuate based on demand. But here's the sweet spot: most partner airlines operate under a fixed award chart with consistently reasonable rates, making them ideal for planning premium-cabin travel. Some top ways to maximize AAdvantage miles include flying: - Economy class domestically from just 7,500 miles, such as from Detroit Metropolitan Wayne County Airport (DTW) to Philadelphia International Airport (PHL) - Economy class to Europe from 25,000 miles on a route like Charlotte Douglas International Airport (CLT) to Dublin Airport (DUB) - Business class from the U.S. to Helsinki Airport (HEL) on Finnair for 57,500 miles - Business class from the West Coast to Japan for 60,000 miles with Japan Airlines - Business class from the U.S. to Australia for 80,000 miles on Qantas Related: How to redeem American Airlines AAdvantage miles for maximum value So, is the 125,000-mile AAdvantage Executive offer one of the best deals ever? As someone who actively collects AAdvantage miles, which we value higher than Delta SkyMiles and United MileagePlus miles, this welcome offer definitely deserves serious consideration for anyone who flies with American Airlines or its partner airlines. The combination of the highest-ever bonus and the card's recent refresh makes this an especially compelling time to apply. Beyond the massive welcome bonus, here are the top five reasons to apply for this card: - Admirals Club membership: You'll get complimentary access to nearly 50 Admirals Clubs worldwide, plus 60-plus partner lounges, and can bring a spouse and children or two guests. This membership alone typically costs $750-$1,400 annually and more than covers the card's $695 fee. - Valuable travel credits: The card offers up to $500 annually in American Airlines Vacations statement credits, up to $180 in Lyft credits*, up to $120 in statement credits for eligible prepaid Avis or Budget car rentals and up to $100 in statement credits for eligible inflight and Admirals Club purchases. - Accelerated mile earning: You'll earn 12 miles per dollar spent on car rentals and hotels booked through American's travel platform, and 4 miles per dollar on eligible AA purchases. - Priority benefits: Save time and money with priority check-in and boarding (for you and up to eight companions, where available), plus complimentary first checked bag on domestic flights. - Elite status: You'll earn complimentary Champion status with Omni Hotels and Presidents Club status with Avis, plus qualify for Loyalty Point bonuses toward AAdvantage elite status. *Up to $15 per month after taking three eligible rides that month Bottom line The Citi / AAdvantage Executive is offering 125,000 bonus AAdvantage miles, the highest welcome offer we've ever tracked on the card. TPG values those miles at $1,813 (based on our valuations), making this a compelling offer for travelers who can comfortably meet the $15,000 spending requirement. Combined with a full Admirals Club membership (worth $750–$1,400 annually) and robust travel perks, the card pays for itself before you even book an award flight. And the redemption options are plentiful: fly domestically in the U.S. for as little as 7,500 miles, or use your AA miles to fly partner airlines like Japan Airlines, Qantas and Cathay Pacific, where fixed award charts make premium cabin bookings surprisingly affordable. Offers this generous don't stick around indefinitely. If you're a loyal American Airlines customer or regularly fly Oneworld carriers, this is the best time to apply. To learn more, check out our full review of the Citi / AAdvantage Executive Mastercard. Apply here: Citi / AAdvantage Executive World Legend Mastercard
